IVR: Thank you for calling Chase Business Card Services. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. For English, press one. Para Español, oprima dos. To continue in English, please remain on the line. Please say or enter the sixteen-digit card number you are calling about. If you do not have your card number, say 'I don't have it'.

IVR: I heard a noise in the background. Please say or enter your card number.

IVR: Okay. In a few words, tell me the reason for your call. You can say things like, 'check a balance', 'report a lost card', or 'dispute a transaction'.

IVR: I'm sorry, I didn't get that. Please tell me the reason for your call. You can say 'agent' at any time to speak to a representative.

IVR: Okay, transferring you to an agent. Please be aware that wait times may be longer than usual. Your business is important to us.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with your Chase Ink Business card? Ask our agent about our latest offers, including an incredible 5x points on dining for a limited time. Don't just do business, do more business, with Chase.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached Chase Business Services, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, I hope you can. I’ve been having a terrible time with my card. It’s completely locked, I think.

AGENT: I can definitely look into that for you. I'm sorry to hear you're having trouble. First, I just need to verify your identity. Can I get your full name, please?

CUSTOMER: Hannah Nguyen. That’s H-A-N-N-A-H, Nguyen is N-G-U-Y-E-N.

AGENT: Thank you, Ms. Nguyen. And just for security, can you please confirm your date of birth?

CUSTOMER: It’s [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Just pulling up your account now. My system is being a little slow today, apologies. Classic Monday morning, even though it’s… what is it, Tuesday?

CUSTOMER: Ugh, tell me about it. It’s a hot one here in Phoenix today. Already feels like a furnace outside.

AGENT: I hear that. It’s actually pretty nice up here for once. We had that big storm last night but it’s cleared up. So, you’re in Phoenix? Did you catch the Granite Falls Miners game over the weekend? What a nail-biter.

CUSTOMER: Oh, we did! My wife was screaming at the TV. I can’t believe they pulled it out in the ninth.

AGENT: Right? I thought for sure they were done for. Okay, looks like my system is finally cooperating. Thank you for your patience. So, I’m looking at the Chase Ink Business Cash card ending in, uh, one-seven-nine-one. Is that the correct one?

CUSTOMER: Yes, star-one-seven-nine-one. That’s the one. It just… it stopped working. I was in Tokyo for a conference, I have a travel notice on file for that, and I tried to buy a train ticket and it was declined. Then I tried to add it to my phone wallet, and that didn't work either. It’s very embarrassing.

AGENT: Oh, I can certainly understand that would be frustrating, especially when you're traveling internationally. Let me see here. Okay, I’m looking at the account notes… just one moment while I read through this. Hmm. Okay. I see a few things here.

CUSTOMER: Okay…

AGENT: Right, so it looks like the system placed a security lock on the card on September fourth.

CUSTOMER: The fourth? Why? What happened?

AGENT: Well, our automated fraud detection system picked up on some unusual activity. It looks like there were two sign-in attempts to your online account, one from your home base in Phoenix, Arizona, and another one just a few minutes later from Miami, Florida.

CUSTOMER: Miami? I haven't been to Miami in years. That wasn't me.

AGENT: Okay, that’s what it looked like to the system. And right after that, there was a purchase attempted at a store in Miami… let’s see… Northgate Camera & Audio, for a pretty high amount. The first time it was declined and a text was sent to your mobile on file asking if it was a legitimate charge.

CUSTOMER: I… I think I remember that. I was in a meeting, I saw a text, and I just replied 'Y' because I thought maybe my wife, Renata, was buying something for the business. She’s on the account.

AGENT: I understand. Well, after that 'Y' reply, the charge was approved. But because of the strange login pattern—the two cities so close together—the system put an automated security lock on the card as a precaution, just to make sure nothing else could get through.

CUSTOMER: Oh my god. So that's why it was declined at H-E-B later that day? I tried to call in about that but I got stuck in the phone menu and hung up.

AGENT: Yes, I see a note about that call attempt as well. And that would also be why the transaction in Tokyo and the attempt to add the card to your Samsung Pay were declined. The note says the error was 'CARD_STATUS_LOCKED_RESTRICTED'. So the lock is definitely still active.

CUSTOMER: So… can you take it off? It was a mistake, I guess, that Miami charge. But the rest is me. I’m the one in Tokyo.

AGENT: I really wish I could, Ms. Nguyen. I can see your approved travel notice for Japan right here, so that all makes sense. However, because this lock was placed by our top-level Fraud and Security department, I don't actually have the tools to remove it myself. It's what we call a hard lock, and it requires a review from that specific team.

CUSTOMER: You’re kidding me. So I’m stuck without my primary business card?

AGENT: I’m so sorry. I know how inconvenient this is. What I need to do is open an escalation case for you. This will get all the information over to the Security team, and they'll be able to investigate and remove the lock. I can do that for you right now.

CUSTOMER: Okay… I guess that’s the only option.

AGENT: Yes, ma'am. Let me just get this started. Okay… just typing up the notes for them. I'm referencing the concurrent login, the charge in Miami, and your confirmation that the activity in Japan was legitimate. The case number for your reference is CASE-4677706.

CUSTOMER: Okay… CASE-4677706. Got it. So what happens now? Do they call me?

AGENT: They will. We can schedule a callback for you. That team works standard business hours, so what's the best date and number for them to reach you?

CUSTOMER: Uh, well I’m back in Phoenix now. Let’s see… Today is the seventh. Can they call on the tenth? September 10, 2026.

AGENT: Absolutely. September 10, 2026. And what’s the best number?

CUSTOMER: They can call my office landline. It’s 602-555-0195. Sorry, wait, I always do that. It’s 602-555-0159. The last two digits are five-nine.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me just correct that. Okay, so I have a callback scheduled for you on September 10, 2026, to the number 602-555-0159. And that’s a landline, not a mobile, correct? We won't be able to text it.

CUSTOMER: Correct, it’s my office landline.

AGENT: Perfect. And listen, Ms. Nguyen, for all the trouble this has caused you, especially while you were traveling, I'd like to go ahead and apply a $20.00 courtesy credit to your account. I know it doesn't solve the problem right now, but I want to apologize for the inconvenience. Let me just try to process that for you... okay, one moment. While that’s loading, was there anything else I could help you with today?

CUSTOMER: Oh. Uh, wait, yes. Actually. While I have you. I was looking at my statement online when I was trying to figure all this out, and there’s another charge I don’t recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with that. Can you give me the details?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, I have it right here. Um… at first I thought it was at Macy's? But no, that’s not it. Let me scroll… here. It’s for $190.14. The merchant says… Lakeview Pet Grooming?

AGENT: Lakeview Pet Grooming. And the amount was $190.14?

CUSTOMER: Yes, one-nine-zero-point-one-four. And it says it’s in Spokane, Washington. I have never been to Spokane in my life. We don’t even have a pet!

AGENT: Okay, I see that charge on my end as well. And just to confirm, you had your card in your possession on the date of that charge?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I did. I mean, my wife has her card too, but she was with me. Her card works fine, by the way, the one ending in 8616. This charge isn't on her card. It’s on mine. And neither of us made it.

AGENT: Understood. And you didn't authorize anyone else to use the card for this purchase?

CUSTOMER: No, definitely not.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. I'm going to file a dispute for this charge. It's a fairly standard process. We’ll credit the amount back to your account temporarily while we investigate with the merchant. Just let me fill out the form here. Let’s see… okay. It’s important to keep your account in good standing during a dispute, so just a general reminder from my script here, uh, that any undisputed balances should be paid on time to avoid interest, and late payments can incur a late fee of up to $40.00. That’s just a general notice.

CUSTOMER: Right, of course.

AGENT: Okay, I have filed that for you. The dispute reference number is DSP-8451719. I've filed it under our internal reason code DISPUTE_RC_13.3, which is for 'Card Not Present' fraud claims. You should see a temporary credit for the $190.14 post to your account within one to two business days.

CUSTOMER: Great. At least that’s something.

AGENT: Yes. Oh, and Ms. Nguyen, one last thing. I was trying to apply that $20.00 courtesy credit for you… and it looks like the system has rejected it. It seems I can't apply any manual credits while the main security lock is on the account. I am so, so sorry about that. I really thought it would go through.

CUSTOMER: Of course it did. It’s just been one of those weeks. It’s fine, don’t worry about it. Just… make sure that security team calls me.

AGENT: I have triple-checked the callback details. They will definitely be in touch. So, to recap: I've opened case CASE-4677706 for the security team to investigate and remove the lock on your card. They will call you at your office landline, 602-555-0159, on September 10, 2026. And I've also filed dispute DSP-8451719 for the $190.14 charge from Lakeview Pet Grooming in Spokane, WA, which you should see credited back temporarily. Your card ending in one-seven-nine-one does remain locked for now.

CUSTOMER: Okay. I guess that’s all we can do. Thank you for your help, Alex.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Ms. Nguyen. I’m sorry again we couldn't fully resolve it on this call. Thank you for your patience, and thank you for calling Chase. Have a good rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

cust_synth_001:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Hannah Nguyen came in just after the lunch rush today, maybe around 1:30 PM. Very pleasant interaction. She’s not from around here, mentioned she’s in town visiting her sister for a few weeks and was enjoying the slightly cooler weather we’re having, which made me laugh. She came over to my desk and I offered her a coffee from the new machine. She actually remembered the old one we had and said this new one is a huge improvement, which is exactly what I've been telling management. We chatted for a minute about her drive over to the Westgate Commons branch; she was coming from the north side of town and was surprised at how light the traffic was. I told her she got lucky.

We also got talking about the Bay City Herons, of all things. I was wearing my Herons pin and she noticed it right away. Turns out she’s a huge fan and follows all the games even though she lives out of state. We both think the new shortstop is a game-changer but we’re a little worried about the bullpen getting tired so early in the season. She’s optimistic, which was nice to hear. It’s always fun when you connect with a customer about something other than banking.

Anyway, she was here to make a pretty substantial payment on her Chase Ink Business Cash (*1791) card. She had a cashier's check with her and handed it over. The purpose of the visit was to apply the full amount of the check to her outstanding balance. I took the check and started keying in the transaction. I must have been thinking about the Herons' starting lineup or something, because I made a clumsy typo and entered the payment as $3,350.00. I was moving through the screens and just before I hit the final confirmation, I glanced down at the physical check on my desk to double-check. That's when I saw my mistake. My face must have given it away because she asked if everything was alright.

I laughed it off and apologized, pointing to the number on my screen and then the number on her check. I told her I’d accidentally transposed a couple of digits and that I’m glad I have a habit of checking everything three times. She was very nice about it, said not to worry. I voided the initial entry and started over, this time very deliberately keying in the correct amount of $3,530.00. I turned my monitor so she could see and had her confirm the amount was correct before proceeding. She gave me the thumbs up and we moved on.

This is the part where I made my own second, minor error of the day. I initially told her that because she was using a cashier's check, the payment would credit to her available balance pretty much immediately, and that she should see same-day availability. That’s often true, but I spoke too soon. When I processed the corrected payment for $3,530.00, the system flagged it and placed a standard hold on the funds. An alert popped up on my screen. I had to backtrack and explain the situation to her, which is never my favorite thing to do. I apologized again and explained that my initial statement was incorrect, and that for certain check deposits, including cashier’s checks, the system automatically applies a hold to ensure the funds clear from the issuing bank. I reassured her this was a standard procedure and not a reflection on her or her account history. She asked how long the hold would be, so I showed her the confirmation screen. The funds from this specific payment are on hold until July 18, 2026. To give her more context, I explained that our policy for cashier's checks over $7,500.00 can sometimes involve even longer holds, so this was just the system operating as designed for a payment of this type. She was perfectly understanding. I printed out her receipt, highlighted the confirmation number BRC-4493749 for her, and made sure she had it for her business records.

Just as she was gathering her things, she paused and said she had one more question. She asked about her wife, Renata. She wanted to know if she could also make a payment on Renata’s card for her while she was here. She mentioned the card ending was 9764. I had to explain our privacy policy, that I couldn't even look up Renata’s account, let alone process a payment from a third party, even a spouse. I told Ms. Nguyen that Renata would need to visit a branch herself with her ID, or that she could easily make the payment herself online or through the mobile app. She said she figured as much but thought she'd ask. She said she'd just tell Renata to handle it online when she got home. She thanked me for my help and for the coffee. We wished each other a good rest of the week and hoped the Bay City Herons would pull off a win this weekend.

Follow-up:
None required. Customer's payment was processed and all questions were answered. Customer was understanding about the funds hold and the policy regarding her wife's account. No further action is needed on my part.

cust_synth_003:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Kwame Kaplan came into the Harborside Market branch this afternoon, maybe around 2:30 PM. I recognized him, I think he was in a few months ago to ask about mortgage rates. He was wearing a Bay City Herons cap and I commented on their recent winning streak, and we got to talking about the season. He's a huge fan, much more than I am, but it's hard not to get caught up in it when they're finally playing well. He thinks they have a real shot this year. We spent a good five minutes on that before we even got down to business. I offered him a coffee from our new machine—everyone's been commenting on it—but he said he was all set. He mentioned he was just passing through on his way home to San Diego and was surprised traffic wasn't worse, so he decided to stop in.

He said the reason for his visit was to make a fairly large payment on his Chase Slate Edge card (*6878). He had a cashier's check with him. I pulled up his profile, verified his ID, and took the check from him. Looking it over, I told him that since it was a cashier's check, we could get that posted immediately and that it should have same-day availability on his account, which would free up his credit line right away. He seemed pleased about that. I began the payment process through the teller system, navigating to the credit card payment screen.

This is where I made a bit of a clumsy mistake. The amount was specific, and I think my fingers just got the numbers jumbled. I typed in the payment as $4,740.00. Thankfully, our branch procedure is to always verify the amount on the screen against the physical check before hitting the final confirmation. When I did my check, I saw the error immediately. I laughed and said something like, "Whoops, looks like I got a little ahead of myself," and showed him where I'd transposed the numbers. The actual amount on the check was clearly $4,470.00. I corrected the entry in the system to the proper $4,470.00. Mr. Kaplan was very good-natured about it, said it was no problem at all.

After correcting the amount, I submitted the transaction. This is the other part that got a bit awkward. The system processed the payment, but then a notification popped up informing me that a standard hold would be placed on the funds. I had to walk back what I'd just told him about same-day availability. The system confirmed the funds would be held until July 14, 2026. I apologized to him and explained that I had misspoken earlier. I turned my monitor so he could see the screen and explained that while the payment itself was successfully posted against his balance, his available credit wouldn't reflect the payment until the hold released on that date. I explained that this is a standard, automated security measure for cashier's checks to ensure they clear properly. He was understandably a little frustrated and asked why I'd said otherwise. I just had to be upfront and say that I was mistaken and that the system policy is the final word. To provide a bit more context on our policies, I mentioned that for especially large checks, for instance amounts over $7,500.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer, so this was a typical hold period. He seemed to accept the explanation, even if he wasn't happy about it. I printed out his receipt, making sure to point out the correct payment amount and the transaction number, BRC-1471588, for his records.

Just as we were wrapping up, he asked if he could also make a payment for his partner, Casey. He said Casey has a card with us and he had the card number, or at least the end of it, which he said was 9685. I had to explain that due to privacy and security policies, I couldn't process a payment for a third party who wasn't present to provide identification. I told him that Casey would either need to come into a branch themselves, or more conveniently, they could make a payment anytime through the app or online banking. He was totally fine with that, said he was just asking because Casey had asked him to. It was just an inquiry, so no action was taken on that.

We ended the visit on a positive note. I apologized one last time for the mix-up with the funds hold, and we chatted for another minute about the Bay City Herons and the upcoming game he was planning to attend. I wished him a safe drive back down to San Diego and he was on his way.

Follow-up:
No immediate follow-up needed. Customer was informed about the funds hold until July 14, 2026 for the cashier's check payment. He seemed to understand the policy after the initial confusion. No other actions are required on my end.

Thanks again for everything, Sarah. Have a wonderful weekend.

All the best,
Kwame Kaplan

[10:45] Customer: yeah the statement was dated January 22, 2025 and the fee was for $32.00

[10:46] Customer: normally i'm totally on top of it. or my sister yuki helps me keep track of household bills when i'm travelling but she was at the wedding too obviously. she's the organised one, her number is 512-555-0359, but we both dropped the ball this time.

[10:47] Agent (Dana): Thank you for that information, and for the explanation. I see the $32.00 late fee from the January 22, 2025 statement period. I understand that things can get hectic with travel and family events.

[10:47] Agent (Dana): Let me see what I can do for you. Please give me one moment to review your account details.

[10:49] Agent (Dana): Thank you for waiting, Rafael. I can see you have a long history of on-time payments with us. As a one-time courtesy, I would be happy to reverse that late fee for you.

[10:49] Customer: oh wow really?

[10:49] Customer: that would be amazing

[10:50] Customer: thank you SO much dana

[10:51] Customer: you have no idea what a relief that is. i was so annoyed at myself for missing it.

[10:51] Customer: really appreciate you doing that for me. that's fantastic customer service.

[10:52] Agent (Dana): It's my pleasure, Rafael. We appreciate your business and we're happy to help. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

[10:52] Customer: no that is everything! you've solved all my problems.

[10:53] Customer: thanks again and have a great day

[10:53] Agent (Dana): You're very welcome, and you too! Thank you for using Chase Secure Chat.

[10:53] Agent (Dana): This chat session will now end.

cust_synth_004:LM1_CALL.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Card Services. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. To continue in English, press one. Para español, oprima dos. Please say or enter your sixteen-digit card number.

IVR: Thank you. For security, please say or enter your date of birth.

IVR: Thank you. Please listen carefully as our menu options have recently changed. For account balance and recent transactions, say 'Balance'. To make a payment, say 'Payment'. To report a card lost or stolen, say 'Lost Card'. For all other inquiries, or to speak with a representative, say 'Agent' or stay on the line.

IVR: Please hold while we connect you to the next available agent. Your current wait time is approximately two minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more rewards? Apply for our Premier Rewards card today and get a $200.00 statement credit after you spend one thousand dollars in the first three months. Plus, earn three percent back on dining and travel. Visit our website to learn more and apply. We appreciate your patience. An agent will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. You've reached Card Services, my name is David. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, my name is Aisha Kaplan.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Kaplan. Thank you for calling. I see you've entered your card number, the Amazon Prime Visa ending in *6966. Just to be sure I'm speaking with the account holder, could you please verify your date of birth for me?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's... [date of birth stated].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. One moment while my system pulls up your details. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: I am hoping you can. My card is locked. I'm… I'm actually traveling right now, I'm in Sydney, and it's just not working anywhere. It's been a complete nightmare. It got declined trying to buy a train ticket, and then I tried to add it to my watch, to the Garmin Pay thing, and that didn't work either. It just said it was restricted.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly understand how frustrating that must be, especially while you're traveling. I'm very sorry for the trouble this is causing. Let me take a look at the account here and see what's going on with that card. Sometimes the system can be a little slow when I'm first pulling up an account, especially with a security flag on it.

CUSTOMER: Take your time, I guess. It’s not like I can go anywhere.

AGENT: Heh, right. Well, while this is loading… are you from Philly? I see a Philadelphia address here.

CUSTOMER: I am, born and raised.

AGENT: Nice. Did you happen to catch the Herons game last night? What a disaster.

CUSTOMER: Ugh, don't remind me. We were watching it at a pub here, it was on at a ridiculous time in the morning. I can't believe they blew that lead in the ninth. It's just classic Bay City Herons, you know?

AGENT: Tell me about it. I thought for sure they had it locked down. The weather over there looked brutal, too. It's been so gray and rainy here, I was jealous of that sunshine.

CUSTOMER: Oh, it's beautiful here, which almost makes it worse. I want to be out doing things, not stuck on the phone with my bank. No offense.

AGENT: None taken, Ms. Kaplan. I completely get it. Okay, looks like I have your account information up now. I do see a security lock was placed on the card. Let me just read through the notes here to get the full picture. One moment. *[typing sounds]*

CUSTOMER: Okay.

AGENT: Okay, so I'm seeing a few different things here. It looks like this all started back on… let's see… on September 10th. Our automated security system detected two login sessions to your online account that happened very close together, one from Philadelphia and another from Tampa, Florida.

CUSTOMER: Tampa? I... oh. Wait. Yes, my husband was in Tampa for work. He was probably logging in to check something.

AGENT: That would make sense. Well, right after those logins, there was a purchase attempted for one thousand, two hundred and forty dollars at a store called Harborview Computers in Tampa. The system initially declined it and sent a text message to the mobile number on file to verify.

CUSTOMER: Yes! I remember that. He called me, I got the text, and I replied 'Y' for yes. It was for a new work laptop for him. Did it not go through? He has the laptop.

AGENT: It looks like the second attempt after you replied was approved, so the purchase did go through successfully. However, because of the, uh, the unusual activity pattern—the concurrent logins from different states and the large dollar amount—the fraud detection system placed an automated security lock on the card as a precaution. It's called a 'containment' measure.

CUSTOMER: But I said it was okay! I verified it! Why would it lock the card if I literally told you it was a legitimate purchase?

AGENT: I understand your confusion, and that is a very good question. In these specific 'velocity' alert situations, the system is designed to approve the verified charge but then restrict the card to prevent any potential follow-on fraudulent activity until we can be sure everything is secure. It’s meant to protect you, even if it is, I admit, very inconvenient in a case like this.

CUSTOMER: Inconvenient is one word for it. So I've been stuck in Australia for two days with a locked card because my husband bought a laptop in Florida?

AGENT: It appears so. I also see a note here that you called our automated phone line later that same day about a declined purchase at a Trader Joe's?

CUSTOMER: Yes! I was trying to buy groceries. It was so embarrassing. The automated system asked for a code it texted me, but I was flustered and I think I just hung up.

AGENT: Yes, the note says the verification wasn't completed on that call, so the restriction remained in place. And that's why the card is still locked now, and why it failed in Sydney. The system notes confirm you have a travel notice on file for Australia, so it knows you're there, but this specific type of security lock overrides that.

CUSTOMER: This is ridiculous. Can you please, please just unlock it for me?

AGENT: Ms. Kaplan, I truly wish I could. Unfortunately, this specific 'SECURITY_LOCKED' restriction is what we call a complex lock. It requires review and removal by our back-office Fraud and Security Operations team. The agents on this line, myself included, we don't have the system permissions to override it. I am very sorry.

CUSTOMER: You're kidding me. So what am I supposed to do?

AGENT: What I can do is open a case to have them review it and remove the lock. I will mark it as urgent due to your travel situation. I'll get that started for you right now. The case number for your reference will be CASE-9581021.

CUSTOMER: CASE-9581021. Okay. And how long does that take?

AGENT: They typically action these within one to two business days. To make sure you get a resolution, I can schedule a direct callback for you from a specialist on that team. The earliest I can book that for is September 16, 2026. Will that work for you?

CUSTOMER: The 16th? I guess it has to. Can they call me on my office number? I'll be back by then. I don't want to miss the call.

AGENT: Absolutely. What is the best number for that callback?

CUSTOMER: It's my landline at work. It's 215-555-0345... no, sorry, that's the main line. My direct line. Hold on. It's 215-555-0354.

AGENT: Okay, got it. I have the callback scheduled for September 16, 2026, to the number 215-555-0354. And I've noted that it's an OFFICE LANDLINE.

CUSTOMER: Thank you. Ugh. While I have you on the line, there was something else. I was looking at my statement online before I called, and there's a charge I don't recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, I can definitely help you with that. Do you have the details there?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, I have it pulled up. It was for $117.85. I... I think it was at Ross Dress for Less? No, wait, that's not it, that's the line above. Sorry. Let me scroll. Okay, here it is. The charge for $117.85 is from a place called Summit Ridge Ski Rentals.

AGENT: Summit Ridge Ski Rentals, okay. And the date of that charge?

CUSTOMER: August 28th.

AGENT: And the location? Does it say on the statement?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it says Pittsburgh, PA. I have never been skiing in my life, and I definitely wasn't in Pittsburgh in August. That's not me. It's so weird, my sister Yuki was just using her card, the one ending in 5644, and it works fine. It's just my card that has all these problems.

AGENT: I understand. We can certainly dispute that charge for you as not authorized. One moment while I pull up the dispute form. *[typing sounds]* Okay, I am filing a dispute for the charge of $117.85 at Summit Ridge Ski Rentals in Pittsburgh, PA. I'm going to file this with reason code DISPUTE_RC_12.6, which is for 'Cardholder Not Present, No Authorization'. We will issue a temporary credit for that amount to your account while the investigation is underway.

CUSTOMER: Okay, thank you.

AGENT: Your reference number for this dispute is DSP-9305819.

CUSTOMER: DSP... 9305819. Got it.

AGENT: Perfect. Ms. Kaplan, I know this has been an incredibly frustrating experience, and I sincerely apologize for the series of issues you've encountered. For the inconvenience of the card being locked and you having to call in like this, I'd like to offer you a $35.00 courtesy credit. I'm just going to apply that to your account right now, one moment. *[typing sounds]*

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thank you. I appreciate that.

AGENT: You are very welcome. Just give me one... huh. That's odd. Oh. Ms. Kaplan, I am so sorry. It appears the same security lock on the account that's blocking transactions is also preventing me from posting a manual credit. My system just rejected the request. I'm afraid I won't be able to apply that $35.00 credit until the main restriction is lifted. I'll add a note to the case for the specialist to apply it when they call you. I feel terrible about that.

CUSTOMER: Of course it did. It's just my luck today. Okay. Just... just make sure they see the note.

AGENT: I absolutely will. I've added it in bold to CASE-9581021. So, to recap: your card is currently under a security lock which I cannot remove, but I have opened case CASE-9581021 for the security team to review and resolve. I've scheduled a callback for you on September 16, 2026, to your office landline, 215-555-0354. And I have filed dispute DSP-9305819 for the $117.85 charge, which will be investigated. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that's it. That's more than enough.

AGENT: I understand completely. Just as a standard reminder, please be aware that payments are due on your statement due date, and late payments can incur a late fee of up to $41.00. Thank you again for your patience today, Ms. Kaplan. I hope the rest of your trip to Sydney improves.

CUSTOMER: Thanks. Me too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: Thank you.

AGENT: Okay, I do see the declines you're referring to. The first one was at a place called... let me see... Seoul Metro Bistro. And then a second one shortly after at Seoul Old Town Market. Is that correct?

AGENT: Let me just confirm the number it was sent to... It was sent to the primary mobile number on your account, ending in 1-8-2-1.

AGENT: Got it. Scheduling a callback for September 12, 2026, to the number 512-555-0869. And I've specified it's an office landline. Okay, that's confirmed. CUSTOMER: Okay, thanks.

AGENT: I can certainly help you with that, sir. Do you have the statement there?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, I have the PDF open. Let me just find it... it was... I think it was at Kohl's? Or something like that. For around a hundred dollars.

AGENT: Okay, looking for a charge from Kohl's...

CUSTOMER: No, wait, here it is. My mistake. It says, P-I-N-E-C-R-E-S-T. Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. The charge is for $109.83. And the location says Pittsburgh, PA. I've never even been to Pittsburgh in my life.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for clarifying. So that's a charge for $109.83 at Pinecrest Outdoor Supply in Pittsburgh, PA. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: That is one hundred percent correct. It wasn't me.

AGENT: Not a problem. We can definitely dispute that for you. I'm opening a dispute claim now. Just while I'm filling this out, I'm required to read a standard disclosure. Just so you are aware, for our general policies, if a payment is late, it can incur a late fee of up to $41.00. That's just a generic notification and doesn't apply to your current situation. Okay, I've got the claim form ready. I'm filing this as a transaction you do not recognize.

CUSTOMER: Correct.

AGENT: Okay, that has been submitted. The dispute reference number is DSP-8870309. For our internal records, the reason code is DISPUTE_RC_10.4. You should see a temporary, provisional credit for the $109.83 post to your account within the next one to two business days while our investigations team looks into it.

CUSTOMER: Okay, good. At least something got done.

AGENT: Yes, sir. So, just to recap our call today: we've identified that your card was temporarily blocked due to international transactions attempted before your travel notice was active, and because a security text to an old number went unanswered. I've opened case CASE-4685268 to have our fraud team urgently review and remove this block. I've scheduled a callback for you on September 12, 2026, to your office number, 512-555-0869, to follow up. And finally, we've successfully filed dispute DSP-8870309 for the $109.83 charge from Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, Mr. Whitfield?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s it. I just hope that fraud team is actually as urgent as you say they are.

AGENT: I've done everything I can from my side to prioritize it, sir. Thank you for your call today, and again, my sincere apologies for the difficult experience.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, okay. Thanks. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye, Mr. Whitfield.

cust_synth_005:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Rafael Whitfield came into the Harborside Market branch around 2 PM. It was a pretty quiet afternoon for once. I was just finishing up some paperwork and saw him looking a little lost over by the deposit slips, so I waved him over to my desk. He seemed relieved. I asked him if he wanted a coffee, mentioning we just got this new fancy machine that everyone's been raving about. He laughed and said sure, why not. While it was brewing I asked what brought him in today. He said he was visiting from Austin, TX, and just needed to make a quick payment on his credit card. His commute to the branch had been a bit of an adventure, apparently he wasn't used to the local traffic patterns and his GPS took him on a very "scenic" route.

He got his coffee (said it was surprisingly good for a bank) and we got down to business. He pulled out his wallet and a cashier's check. I asked for his ID, which he provided, and pulled up his profile. He wanted to make a payment toward his Chase Freedom Unlimited (*2673). I took the cashier's check from him and, I have to admit, I was a little distracted because I noticed he had a Granite Falls Miners keychain. I'm a huge fan, and their season has been an absolute rollercoaster. I asked him if he was a fan and he lit up. We spent a good five minutes talking about the last game and whether the new pitcher is going to be the real deal or not. He thinks they've got a solid chance to go all the way this year, and I've got to say I agree. It's just nice to meet a fellow fan, you don't see many around here.

Anyway, I finally turned my full attention back to the transaction. I glanced at the check and keyed in the payment amount. "Okay, Mr. Whitfield, so we're making a payment of $2,920.00 today," I said, about to hit confirm. As I said it, I looked down at the physical check on my desk to double-check, and my heart sank a little. Whoops. My fingers had totally gotten ahead of my brain. "Oh, hold on a moment," I said, laughing it off. "Apologies, I must have the Miners on my mind. I transposed the numbers. Let me correct that for you right now." I cancelled the entry and very carefully re-keyed the correct amount. "Let's try that again. A payment of $2,290.00." He was good-natured about it and said it was no problem.

I processed the payment for the corrected $2,290.00. I told him, "Since this is a cashier's check, we should see same-day availability for you, so the payment will post right away." The system spun for a moment, and then a little yellow flag popped up on my screen. Of course. I had to immediately walk back what I just said, which is always my favorite thing to do. "Actually, Mr. Whitfield, my apologies again. It looks like the system has automatically placed a standard regulatory hold on the funds. I spoke too soon." I explained that even with cashier's checks, the system sometimes places a hold for verification, and that it's a standard policy to protect both him and the bank. I showed him the screen where it detailed the hold. "The funds from this payment will be fully available and credited to your card balance on April 25, 2026." He looked a little confused, so I elaborated. "It's just a procedural delay, sir. In fact, for any cashier's checks over $5,000.00, the hold can sometimes be even longer. This is just the standard timeframe for a check of this amount." He nodded, seeming to understand, if not thrilled. I printed out his receipt and pointed out the confirmation number, BRC-7919774, for his records.

As he was gathering his things, he paused. "You know, while I'm here, can I ask a quick question for my sister? Her name is Yuki." I said of course. "She has one of your cards too, I think the number ends in 1085. She wanted to know if I could find out her current balance for her." I had to explain that due to privacy and security policies, I couldn't access his sister's account information or discuss it with him. I told him that Yuki would need to come into a branch herself with her ID, or she could check her balance any time using the mobile app or by logging in online. He said he understood and would pass the message along. He thanked me for my time and for the coffee, and we wished the Miners good luck for the rest of their season.

Follow-up:
No follow-up actions are required from my end. Customer paid $2,290.00 toward his Chase Freedom Unlimited (*2673) via cashier's check. I informed him of the funds hold until April 25, 2026, and he acknowledged it. Provided privacy-based guidance regarding his sister's (Yuki) account query for a card ending in 1085.

cust_synth_009:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Marcus Lindqvist came into the Harborside Market branch this afternoon, around 2:15 PM. He's a really nice guy, originally from Atlanta, GA, but said he's in town for an extended work project. We got to chatting a bit while my system was loading up after I authenticated him with his driver's license and physically matching him to his profile picture. He complimented our new coffee machine, said the smell was a lot better than the old burnt pot we used to have. I offered him a cup but he said he was trying to cut back. He was wearing a Granite Falls Miners cap, so of course I had to ask him about the season. He's a big fan, says he tries to catch a game whenever he can, thinks they have a real shot this year if the bullpen can just hold it together. I told him I'm more of a baseball person myself but I can appreciate a good underdog story. He was just happy to find someone to talk sports with, said his commute in was a nightmare and he just needed to decompress for a minute.

Mr. Lindqvist's reason for visit was to make a payment on his Chase Freedom Flex card, the one ending in *5997. He had a cashier's check with him. I took the check and his card to process the payment at my terminal. I glanced at the check and started keying everything in. Honestly, it's been a long day and I must have been thinking about that Miners conversation, because I initially typed in the payment amount as $1,820.00. I had it all ready to go on the screen when I did my standard double-check, looking at the physical check in my hand and comparing it to the entry. That's when I saw my mistake. The check was very clearly written for $1,280.00. Big difference! I'm glad I have my little system of checking and re-checking. I backspaced and corrected the amount on my screen to the proper $1,280.00 before proceeding. I didn't mention my fat-finger error to the customer, no need to make him worry that I wasn't paying attention. I just continued on with the transaction as normal.

After inputting the correct amount, I ran the check through the scanner and submitted the payment. While the system was processing, I told him, "Alright, Mr. Lindqvist, we're processing that payment for you now. Since it's a cashier's check, this should post with same-day availability and you'll see your available credit update pretty much immediately." Famous last words. Of course, as soon as I said that, the system flagged it. A little yellow box popped up on my screen indicating a hold would be placed on the funds. I had to walk back what I just said, which is always my favorite thing to do. I said, "Ah, actually, my apologies. It looks like because this is an out-of-state cashier's check, the system is placing a standard hold on the funds just for verification. It's a routine security measure, nothing to be concerned about."

He looked a little disappointed, which is understandable. I pulled up the details of the hold to give him a clear explanation. I showed him on my screen that the hold on the funds from this payment will be released on May 20, 2026. I explained that while the payment is considered received today, the funds won't be fully "available" to the account in the system's eyes until that date. I tried to soften it by explaining the policy, noting that it's a standard procedure for certain types of checks to prevent fraud, and that for very large cashier's checks, say, anything over $10,000.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer. He seemed to understand, just a bit frustrated with the process, which I get. I assured him the payment was accepted and his account was in good standing. I printed out his receipt, number BRC-9326727, and highlighted the payment amount and the confirmation number for his records.

Just as he was about to leave, he paused and asked if he could also make a payment for his brother, Emeka. He said he had the card number or at least the last four digits, which he thought were 3597. I had to explain our privacy policy, that for security reasons we can't process a transaction on an account for someone who isn't present and authenticated, even for a close family member. I told him the easiest thing would be for his brother Emeka to come into a branch himself, or to make the payment online or over the phone. He was fine with that, said he figured as much but it was worth asking. I walked him to the door and we wished the Miners good luck for the rest of their season.

Follow-up:
No immediate action required. Customer was given receipt BRC-9326727 for the $1,280.00 payment. He was informed of the funds hold until May 20, 2026. If customer calls to inquire about the hold, refer to these notes. The situation with his brother's card (ending 3597) was informational only.

Honestly, it's been a long day and I must have been thinking about that Miners conversation, because I initially typed in the payment amount as $1,820.00. I had it all ready to go on the screen when I did my standard double-check, looking at the physical check in my hand and comparing it to the entry. That's when I saw my mistake. The check was very clearly written for $1,280.00. Big difference! I'm glad I have my little system of checking and re-checking. I backspaced and corrected the amount on my screen to the proper $1,280.00 before proceeding. I didn't mention my fat-finger error to the customer, no need to make him worry that I wasn't paying attention. I just continued on with the transaction as normal.

After inputting the correct amount, I ran the check through the scanner and submitted the payment. While the system was processing, I told him, "Alright, Mr. Lindqvist, we're processing that payment for you now. Since it's a cashier's check, this should post with same-day availability and you'll see your available credit update pretty much immediately." Famous last words. Of course, as soon as I said that, the system flagged it. A little yellow box popped up on my screen indicating a hold would be placed on the funds. I had to walk back what I just said, which is always my favorite thing to do. I said, "Ah, actually, my apologies. It looks like because this is an out-of-state cashier's check, the system is placing a standard hold on the funds just for verification. It's a routine security measure, nothing to be concerned about."

He looked a little disappointed, which is understandable. I pulled up the details of the hold to give him a clear explanation. I showed him on my screen that the hold on the funds from this payment will be released on May 20, 2026. I explained that while the payment is considered received today, the funds won't be fully "available" to the account in the system's eyes until that date. I tried to soften it by explaining the policy, noting that it's a standard procedure for certain types of checks to prevent fraud, and that for very large cashier's checks, say, anything over $10,000.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer. He seemed to understand, just a bit frustrated with the process, which I get. I assured him the payment was accepted and his account was in good standing. I printed out his receipt, number BRC-9326727, and highlighted the payment amount and the confirmation number for his records.

Just as he was about to leave, he paused and asked if he could also make a payment for his brother, Emeka. He said he had the card number or at least the last four digits, which he thought were 3597. I had to explain our privacy policy, that for security reasons we can't process a transaction on an account for someone who isn't present and authenticated, even for a close family member. I told him the easiest thing would be for his brother Emeka to come into a branch himself, or to make the payment online or over the phone. He was fine with that, said he figured as much but it was worth asking. I walked him to the door and we wished the Miners good luck for the rest of their season.

No immediate action required. Customer was given receipt BRC-9326727 for the $1,280.00 payment. He was informed of the funds hold until May 20, 2026. If customer calls to inquire about the hold, refer to these notes. The situation with his brother's card (ending 3597) was informational only.

cust_synth_010:LM1_CALL.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Chase Card Services. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. To report a card lost or stolen, press 1. For questions about your account balance or recent transactions, press 2. To speak with a representative, press 0, or stay on the line.

[BEEP]

IVR: Please enter the last four digits of your credit card number, followed by the pound sign.

[BEEP, BEEP, BEEP, BEEP, BEEP]

IVR: Thank you. Please hold while I connect you to the next available agent.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn 75,000 bonus points with the new Chase Sapphire Preferred card after you spend four thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening? That's over nine hundred dollars toward travel when you redeem through Chase Ultimate Rewards. Ask your representative for more details.

[Music on hold plays for approximately two minutes]

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached Chase Card Services, my name is Sarah. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Uh, hi. My name is Marcus Volkov.

AGENT: Hello, Mr. Volkov. I can certainly help you today. For security, could you please verify the full name on the account and your date of birth?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s Marcus Volkov. And the date of birth… do you want me to just say it?

AGENT: Just the month and day is fine, please.

CUSTOMER: Okay. It’s [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. And the billing address, just the street and zip code?

CUSTOMER: [REDACTED], and the zip is [REDACTED].

AGENT: Excellent, thank you so much for that. I’m just pulling up your account now, Mr. Volkov. The system is being a little… a little slow this afternoon, so I appreciate your patience.

CUSTOMER: No problem.

AGENT: While this loads… how’s the weather down there in Charlotte? We’re getting all the rain up here.

CUSTOMER: Oh, you know. It’s hot. Humid. The usual. At least it’s not raining, I guess. We need some for the garden, but… not today.

AGENT: I hear that. Okay, looks like I’m in. I see you have the Chase Sapphire Preferred card with us. How can I help you with the account today?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, so… I’m having a bit of a nightmare here. I lost my wallet, I think last Wednesday? So I called the automated line and reported the card lost. The one ending in… uh… 7240.

AGENT: Okay, I see that. Let me just open up the notes here. One moment… lots of clicking on my end, sorry.

CUSTOMER: It’s fine. So, I reported it lost. And the system said a new one was on its way, you know, five to seven days, whatever. But since then, nothing works. My gym membership, Planet Fitness, they emailed me saying the payment was declined. My wife told me the Peloton charge was declined too. And then yesterday, I was trying to buy lunch at Chipotle, and the tap-to-pay on my phone just… boom. Declined. I thought the digital wallet thing was supposed to keep working.

AGENT: Hmm. Okay. Thank you for that summary, Mr. Volkov, that’s very helpful. I’m just reviewing the account history here and… yes, I can see exactly what you’re describing.

CUSTOMER: So what’s the deal? I haven’t gotten the new card yet, and I feel like I’m just cut off.

AGENT: I completely understand your frustration, and I’m sorry for the inconvenience this has caused. Let me walk you through what I’m seeing on my screen. It looks like on September 16th, you did report the card ending in 7240 as lost. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, Wednesday. That’s right.

AGENT: Okay. So, when that happens, our system immediately closes that card number for your protection. That’s status CARD_CLOSED_LOST on our end. At the same time, it automatically triggers a new card to be issued—that’s the one ending in 4968—and it was sent out via standard mail. The delivery estimate is five to seven business days, so it should be arriving any day now.

CUSTOMER: Right, but what about all the declines?

AGENT: Yes, so, I’m seeing those here. On the 17th, there were two attempts from… let’s see… Planet Fitness and Peloton. Because they were trying to bill the old, closed card number, the system automatically declined them with a CARD_CLOSED response. They won't have the new number until you provide it to them.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I guess that makes sense. But the phone payment? At Chipotle?

AGENT: Right. And that’s the other piece of this. When the physical card is closed, we also revoke the security tokens that are linked to it in digital wallets, like Google Pay. So even though the app was on your phone, the token it was trying to use was connected to the lost 7240 card, which is why that payment was declined with a TOKEN_REVOKED error. You’ll need to add the new card to your digital wallet once you receive it and activate it.

CUSTOMER: So I’m basically just stuck until this piece of plastic shows up in the mail? I can’t pay for anything? That seems… wrong. Can’t you expedite it or something?

AGENT: I do understand, sir. Unfortunately, since the card has already been processed and is in transit with the postal service, I don’t have a way to intercept it or speed up its delivery. I am very sorry about that. What I can do is open an internal investigation to see if there are any other options for you in this situation. I can put in a request with our specialist support team.

CUSTOMER: And what will they do?

AGENT: They’ll review the account and the timeline of events and determine if there was a service failure or if there’s a way to provide you with provisional access to your funds. I can’t make any promises, but I can certainly get the process started for you. Would that be okay?

CUSTOMER: I guess. It’s better than nothing. Did you see the Herons game last night, by the way? Total disaster.

AGENT: Oh, don’t even get me started! That fumble in the third quarter… I almost threw my remote at the TV. Unbelievable. But they’ll bounce back. Okay, so, I am creating the case for you now. The reference number for your records is CASE-8166543.

CUSTOMER: Okay, CASE-8166543. Got it.

AGENT: And I know this whole situation has been a major headache, so for the trouble with the declined payments and everything, I’d like to see if I can apply a courtesy credit to your account. Let me just try to post a $35.00 credit for you. One moment while I submit that.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thanks. I appreciate that.

AGENT: Of course. Just… typing it in here… and… Hmm. Oh, that’s odd. Mr. Volkov, I do apologize. It seems the system has rejected the credit request on my end. I’m not sure why; sometimes it does that when a card is in a transitional state. I will make a strong note in the case file—in CASE-8166543—that I attempted to apply a $35.00 credit and that it should be honored by the specialist team who reviews it. I’m very sorry about that.

CUSTOMER: So, no credit either. Terrific. This is just great.

AGENT: I am truly sorry, sir. Let’s get this callback scheduled so we can get this resolved for you. The specialist team typically responds within two to three business days. I can book a callback for you. What’s the best number to reach you at?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah. Use my office landline. It’s 704-555-0592. Sorry, wait, that’s not right. Hang on. It’s 704-555-0529. Yeah, 0-5-2-9. It’s my OFFICE LANDLINE, so not a mobile.

AGENT: Not a problem at all. Let me just correct that here. So, the best callback number is 704-555-0529. And what would be a good date? I can schedule it for, say, September 25, 2026?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, that’s fine. The 25th works.

AGENT: Perfect. I have scheduled that callback for you. So, just to recap, I’ve opened case CASE-8166543, and a specialist will be calling you back at 704-555-0529 on September 25, 2026. Is there anything else at all I can help you with while I have you on the line?

CUSTOMER: Actually… yeah. Since I’m looking at my statement online now… there’s a charge here I don’t recognize at all. From a few weeks back.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with that. Can you give me the date and amount?

CUSTOMER: Let me see. It’s… it’s for $363.87. I have no idea what that is. I thought maybe it was at Dollar General? My wife sends me there sometimes… but the name doesn’t look right. No, wait, here it is. It says… Crescent Moon Bookshop.

AGENT: Crescent Moon Bookshop, for $363.87. And do you see a location listed, Mr. Volkov?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, that’s the other thing. It says Spokane, WA. I’ve never been to Spokane. Never even been to Washington state. My wife Leonie’s card, the one ending in 6888, that one is working just fine, no strange charges on hers. It’s definitely not one of ours.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. I am initiating a dispute for this charge now. One moment. Just so you are aware for future reference, I am required to inform you that any late payments on an account can incur a late fee of up to $41.00. That’s just a standard disclosure.

CUSTOMER: Right, okay.

AGENT: So, I am filing this charge from Crescent Moon Bookshop in Spokane, WA for $363.87 as not recognized. I’m flagging this as a fraudulent charge. The system is asking for a reason code… let me find the right one… okay, I’m using DISPUTE_RC_12.6. The dispute has been filed. We will issue a temporary credit for the amount while we investigate, which can take up to two billing cycles. Your reference number for this dispute is DSP-3665576.

CUSTOMER: Okay, hold on, let me write that down. D-S-P… 3-6-6-5-5-7-6. Got it.

AGENT: Excellent. So, to summarize our call, Mr. Volkov: we’ve opened case CASE-8166543 regarding your replacement card and the declined transactions, with a callback scheduled to your office landline, 704-555-0529, on September 25, 2026. And we have also filed dispute DSP-3665576 for the $363.87 charge from Crescent Moon Bookshop. Do you have any other questions for me today?

CUSTOMER: No, I think that’s everything. It’s a mess, but… thank you for your help.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Mr. Volkov. I’m confident the specialist team will be able to sort this out for you. Thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you have a much better rest of your day. And go Herons!

CUSTOMER: Heh. Yeah, you too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

IVR: Welcome to Chase. For security and quality purposes, this call may be recorded. To report a lost or stolen card, press 1. To check your account balance, press 2. To speak with a representative, press 3, or stay on the line.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with your Chase Freedom Flex card? For a limited time, get 5x points on dining, including takeout and eligible delivery services. Activate your offer in the Chase mobile app today. An agent will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. You've reached Chase Card Services, my name is Sarah. How can I assist you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, hello. I’m calling about my card. I… I reported it lost over a week ago and the new one still hasn't shown up, and now things are getting declined and it’s… it’s becoming a real problem.

AGENT: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that. I can definitely look into the status of your replacement card for you. For security, can I please start with your full name?

CUSTOMER: Marcus Lindqvist. That’s M-A-R-C-U-S, Lindqvist, L-I-N-D-Q-V-I-S-T.

AGENT: Thank you, Mr. Lindqvist. And could you please verify the date of birth on the account for me?

CUSTOMER: It’s [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Okay, just give me one moment while I pull up your account details here. My system can be a little slow to load sometimes.

CUSTOMER: No problem.

AGENT: So, you're in Atlanta, I see. How's the weather down there today? We're finally getting a bit of a break from the heat up here.

CUSTOMER: Oh man, it's just brutal. You walk outside and it feels like you’re swimming. Just thick, you know? The humidity.

AGENT: I hear that. Sounds like a good day to stay inside. Speaking of which, did you happen to catch the Lakeside Lynx game last night?

CUSTOMER: Oh, don't even get me started. What a heartbreaker. I was there. We were up by two scores in the fourth quarter. I just… I can’t believe they blew that lead. Unbelievable.

AGENT: I know, right? I was shouting at my TV. I thought for sure they had it locked down. Well, hopefully they can pull it together for the next one. Okay, looks like… yep, I've got your account up on my screen now. Thank you for your patience.

CUSTOMER: Sure.

AGENT: Okay, so… let me just review the notes here. I am seeing that on September eleventh, your Chase Freedom Flex card… the one ending in five nine nine seven… was reported lost through our automated phone system. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s right. I was on my way home from work, realized my wallet was gone. Called right away.

AGENT: Okay, that was definitely the right thing to do. So the system immediately closed that card to protect you, and it automatically triggered a new one to be issued. That’s a new Chase Freedom Flex, the card ending in nine one nine three. And it was sent via standard mail to the address we have on file, which should take about five to seven business days.

CUSTOMER: Right, but it's been more than that, hasn't it? Or it feels like it. My gym membership, Planet Fitness, got declined. My Spotify got declined. I tried to buy sushi the other day with the tap-to-pay on my watch and that got declined. It's embarrassing.

AGENT: I can absolutely understand your frustration, Mr. Lindqvist. Looking at the event log here, I do see those declines. It looks like Planet Fitness and Spotify both tried to bill the old, closed card number on the thirteenth. And I also see a Garmin Pay transaction that was declined, also on the thirteenth. That would be your watch. The digital token for your old card was revoked when you reported it lost, so that's why that didn't go through. The new card would need to be added to your digital wallet once you receive and activate it.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, but that’s the whole point. I don’t have it. My brother Emeka, he uses his card all the time, no problem, the one ending in 5734, I think. But I’m just completely stuck. I need my card.

AGENT: I understand completely. Looking at the tracking information for the new card… it was mailed out on the twelfth, and… yes, the system is showing its status as still in transit within the US Postal Service system. Since it was sent by standard mail, that five to seven business day window… today is the sixth business day, so it is still within the expected delivery timeframe, though I know it’s on the longer end of it. Unfortunately, because it's already in the mail stream, there's no way for me to expedite it or track it any more closely from my end.

CUSTOMER: So I just have to wait? What if it got lost in the mail, too?

AGENT: It’s a valid concern. I know this has been a huge inconvenience for you. Let me see what I can do. I… I’m going to see if I can apply a courtesy credit to your account for the trouble. Just one moment, let me try something here… I'm requesting a… a $35.00 credit for the delayed card and service disruption… just a moment…
(typing sounds)
AGENT: Ah. Okay. It looks like… huh. My system is rejecting the credit. I'm very sorry about that, Mr. Lindqvist. It says the account isn't eligible for that specific credit at this time. I do apologize.

CUSTOMER: (Sighs) Of course. Okay. So what now?

AGENT: Well, what I am going to do is open an internal investigation to make sure this is being properly tracked by our card services team. I'm creating a formal case right now, which will escalate this. The case number for your records is CASE-3785761. Again, that’s C-A-S-E, hyphen, three-seven-eight-five-seven-six-one.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I got it.

AGENT: With that case opened, I can also schedule a callback for you from a specialist. If the card doesn't arrive in the next day or so, they will have more tools to resolve this, including potentially express-shipping another replacement. The earliest I can book that appointment for is September 21, 2026. Would a call on that day work for you?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s fine. The twenty-first is a Monday, right? Yeah, that works.

AGENT: Great. And what is the best number for the specialist to reach you at?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yeah, call my office landline. Don’t call my mobile, I might be in a meeting. The number is 404-555-0250… oh, wait, sorry, that’s the main line, they’ll just put you through a directory. My direct line. It's 404-555-0250, sorry, 404-555-0205. The last two digits are zero-five.

AGENT: Okay, let me read that back. A callback on September 21, 2026, to the office landline number 404-555-0205.

CUSTOMER: That’s the one.

AGENT: Perfect. I have that all scheduled for you. Now, while I have you on the line, was there anything else I could help with today?

CUSTOMER: Actually, yes. Since I have you. I was looking at my last online statement, from before I lost the card, and there’s a charge on there I don't recognize at all. It was for like seventy-something dollars. I think it was at Kohl's? Or… wait, let me pull it up on my screen here… hang on… no, not Kohl’s. Here it is. It says the merchant is Pinecrest Outdoor Supply.

AGENT: Okay, Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. And do you have the date and the exact amount of that charge?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, it was on September tenth. The amount is $74.42.

AGENT: Seventy-four dollars and forty-two cents. And you're certain this wasn't a purchase you made?

CUSTOMER: One hundred percent. I’ve never even heard of that store. It says it's in Savannah, GA. I haven’t been to Savannah in years. Definitely not me.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for clarifying. I can absolutely file a transaction dispute for that. One moment while I locate that charge in your history... (typing sounds) ...Okay, I see it right here. September tenth, a charge for $74.42 at Pinecrest Outdoor Supply in Savannah, GA. I am filing the dispute now on the grounds that you do not recognize the transaction. The internal reason code for this will be DISPUTE_RC_13.3.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

AGENT: And for procedural reasons, I just need to read you this standard disclosure. Ahem... 'Please note that late payment of your outstanding balance may result in a late fee of up to $41.00 being applied to your account.' That's just a generic notification for all accounts.

CUSTOMER: Got it.

AGENT: Alright, the dispute has been successfully filed. We'll issue a temporary credit for the charge while we investigate. Your reference number for this dispute is DSP-5865348. That's D-S-P, as in "dispute", hyphen, five-eight-six-five-three-four-eight.

CUSTOMER: Great, thank you.

AGENT: You're welcome. So, just to recap our call, Mr. Lindqvist. We’ve opened case CASE-3785761 to track the delivery of your replacement card. I have booked a specialist callback for you on September 21, 2026, to your office number, 404-555-0205. And finally, we have filed dispute DSP-5865348 for the $74.42 charge from Pinecrest Outdoor Supply. Have I missed anything?

CUSTOMER: No, that covers it. Finally feel like we’re getting somewhere.

AGENT: I'm glad I could help get the ball rolling. Again, I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience with your card and that I couldn't apply that credit for you. But a specialist will be in touch on the twenty-first. Thank you for calling Chase, Mr. Lindqvist.

CUSTOMER: Okay, thank you, Sarah. Bye.

cust_synth_011:LM1_CALL.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. Your call may be recorded for quality and training purposes. To continue in English, press one. Para Español, oprima dos. Please listen carefully as our menu options have recently changed. For information on your account balance or recent transactions, press one. To make a payment, press two. To report a card as lost, stolen, or to inquire about a replacement card, press three. For all other inquiries, press zero to speak with an agent, or stay on the line.

[BEEP]

IVR: Please hold while we connect you to the next available business card specialist. Your estimated wait time is three to five minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with the Chase Ink Business Unlimited card? Earn unlimited 1.5% cash back on every purchase made for your business. Plus, new cardmembers can earn a $200.00 statement credit after you spend three thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Visit Chase dot com to learn more. We appreciate your patience and will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached the Business Card Services department, my name is Maria. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, I... I hope you can. I'm having a lot of trouble with my card. Or my lack of a card, I guess.

AGENT: I'm very sorry to hear that. I can definitely look into it for you. To get started, could I just get your full name, please?

CUSTOMER: Owen Nguyen. That's O-W-E-N, Nguyen, N-G-U-Y-E-N.

AGENT: Thank you, Mr. Nguyen. And just to verify the account, can you please confirm the date of birth associated with the card?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Just give me one moment while my system pulls up your account details. It can be a little slow this afternoon.

CUSTOMER: Take your time.

AGENT: Okay… loading up here. So you’re in Denver, right? Rough game for the Lynx last night, huh?

CUSTOMER: Ugh, don’t remind me. I thought they had it in the third, but that last-minute fumble… painful. Just painful to watch. My son was devastated.

AGENT: I know, my whole family was yelling at the TV. At least the weather’s been nice. We’re finally getting some sun after all that rain.

CUSTOMER: That’s true. Can’t complain about that. Alright, is your, uh, system loaded?

AGENT: Yes, it is. Thank you for your patience. I see the account for Owen Nguyen with the Chase Ink Business Cash card. Which card are we talking about today? Is it the one ending in 3371?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s the one. Or, it *was*. I lost it. I think I left it at a restaurant last week, on Thursday. I called in and reported it lost right away using the automated phone thing.

AGENT: Okay, I see that. Let me check the notes here. Hmm. Yes, I'm seeing a record right here from... let's see... September 3rd. It says the card ending in 3371 was reported lost via the phone banking system.

CUSTOMER: Right. And the system said a new one was on its way. But since then, it’s been a total mess. I got an email that my Spotify subscription was declined. Then another for Adobe. These are business expenses, I need them. And then yesterday I tried to buy lunch using Google Pay on my phone, which is usually linked to that card, and it was declined too. What’s going on? Is the new card not active? Did I do something wrong?

AGENT: No, no, Mr. Nguyen, you did everything correctly. Let me explain what I'm seeing on my end. So, when you reported the card lost on the 3rd, the system immediately closed that card number—the one ending in 3371—to protect you from any fraudulent charges. That’s standard procedure.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that makes sense.

AGENT: At the same time, the system automatically issued a replacement card, which will have a new number. I see that was sent via standard mail, and the typical delivery time is five to seven business days.

CUSTOMER: Five to seven *business* days? So it might not even be here until the end of this week?

AGENT: That’s correct. Looking at the tracking, it currently shows as IN_TRANSIT, so it is on its way to the address we have on file for you in Denver.

CUSTOMER: But what about my payments? The Adobe one is for my whole design team. And the tap-to-pay? I thought that would just... you know, update.

AGENT: I understand your frustration, and I can see here exactly what happened. The recurring charges for Spotify and Adobe were declined because they were trying to bill the old, closed card number. The merchants haven't been provided with the new number yet. Once your new card arrives, you’ll need to log into those services and update your payment information with the new card number and expiration date.

CUSTOMER: Okay. So I just have to wait for the mail. And what about the phone payment? The Google Pay thing?

AGENT: Yes, I see that here as well. A declined tap-to-pay attempt. When the old card was closed, the digital wallet tokens associated with it were also revoked for security. So even though your phone’s wallet looks like it has the card, the link to the actual account was severed. You’ll need to add the new card to your Google Pay wallet once it arrives and you activate it.

CUSTOMER: So basically, I’m just stuck. I can't use my card or my phone for anything until a piece of plastic shows up in my mailbox. It’s a bit ridiculous. My wife, Renata, her business card is working fine, the one ending in 4969. But mine is the primary one we use for all the subscriptions.

AGENT: I do apologize for the inconvenience, Mr. Nguyen. I know it’s not ideal when you’re trying to run a business. The security measures are automatic to protect the account, but it does create this waiting period. There isn’t a way for me to reactivate the old card number or push the new card information to your digital wallet before the physical card arrives.

CUSTOMER: So… you can’t do anything? I waited on hold just to be told to wait some more?

AGENT: I can’t expedite the mail, but what I can do is open a case to have this situation formally documented and reviewed. This will create a record of the disruption to your services. And I can schedule a follow-up call with you to ensure that by a certain date, everything is resolved. How does that sound?

CUSTOMER: A case, okay. I guess that's something.

AGENT: Alright, I'm opening the case now. Just a moment… Okay. The reference number for this is CASE-9879276. And I can schedule a specialist to call you back to make sure you've received the card and that your digital wallet and recurring payments are getting sorted. The earliest I can book that is for September 10, 2026. Would that work for you? That should give enough time for the card to arrive.

CUSTOMER: September 10th… Yeah, fine. Let’s do that.

AGENT: Great. And what is the best number for us to reach you at for that callback?

CUSTOMER: Uh, just my office landline. It's 303-555-0309. Wait, no, sorry, I always mix that up. It's 303-555-0390.

AGENT: Okay, I have that down. A callback scheduled for September 10, 2026, to your office landline, 303-555-0390. And I'll note that it's a landline, not a mobile.

CUSTOMER: Good. Oh, hey, while I have you on the line, there was something else. I was looking at my last statement before all this happened, and there’s a charge I don't recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with a dispute. Do you have the details?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, hold on, I have the PDF open here. It was for… I think it was at Dollar General? No, that’s not it, that was the line above. Here it is. It says ‘Brightline Fitness Club’. For $669.35.

AGENT: Brightline Fitness Club. And the amount was six hundred sixty-nine dollars and thirty-five cents?

CUSTOMER: That’s it. And the location says Pittsburgh, PA. I’ve never even been to Pittsburgh. We’re in Denver. It makes no sense.

AGENT: I see. And you don’t recognize this charge at all? No one else authorized on the account would have made this purchase?

CUSTOMER: No, it's just me on this card. It's definitely not mine.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. I’m initiating a dispute for you now. Just to be clear for the record, you are disputing the charge of $669.35 from Brightline Fitness Club in Pittsburgh, PA. I'm filing this under our standard code for a charge from an unknown merchant, which is DISPUTE_RC_13.1.

CUSTOMER: Whatever the code is, as long as I don’t have to pay for someone else’s gym membership.

AGENT: Absolutely. The process is that we will issue a temporary credit for the amount while we investigate. The investigation can take some time, but we’ll contact the merchant and get to the bottom of it. You'll see the temporary credit on your account within one to two billing cycles. Just be aware that if a payment is late for any reason, it can incur a late fee of up to $39.00, so it's good you're addressing this now.

CUSTOMER: Right, okay.

AGENT: Your dispute reference number is DSP-2462284. You should also receive a letter in the mail outlining the next steps. And you know what, Mr. Nguyen, for all the trouble you’ve been through with the card replacement and the declined payments, I’d like to offer you a $30.00 courtesy credit for the inconvenience. I can apply that to your account right now.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thanks. I appreciate that.

AGENT: Of course. Just give me one second to process that for you... I'm just typing in the reason code here... and applying the credit... hmm. That's odd. Ah, it looks like… hmm. It looks like the system isn't letting me apply that credit right now, Mr. Nguyen. I'm very sorry, it seems you're not eligible at this time for a courtesy credit. I do apologize for offering that.

CUSTOMER: You’re kidding me. So you offer me something and then take it back? This whole call has been one thing after another.

AGENT: I am sincerely sorry about that. The system has final say, and I shouldn't have spoken too soon. I truly apologize for the frustration this has caused.

CUSTOMER: Unbelievable. Fine. Just… just make sure that dispute is filed and the callback is scheduled.

AGENT: I can absolutely confirm that for you. I have successfully filed dispute DSP-2462284 for the charge from Brightline Fitness Club. And I have you scheduled for a callback on September 10, 2026. The overall issue is being tracked under case number CASE-9879276. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No. No, that’s more than enough for one day. Thanks. I guess.

AGENT: I understand. Thank you again for calling Chase Business Card Services, Mr. Nguyen. I hope the rest of your day is better.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, you too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.
