To report a card as lost, stolen, or to inquire about a replacement card, press three. For all other inquiries, press zero to speak with an agent, or stay on the line.

[BEEP]

IVR: Please hold while we connect you to the next available business card specialist. Your estimated wait time is three to five minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with the Chase Ink Business Unlimited card? Earn unlimited 1.5% cash back on every purchase made for your business. Plus, new cardmembers can earn a $200.00 statement credit after you spend three thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Visit Chase dot com to learn more. We appreciate your patience and will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you've reached the Business Card Services department, my name is Maria. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, I... I hope you can. I'm having a lot of trouble with my card. Or my lack of a card, I guess.

AGENT: I'm very sorry to hear that. I can definitely look into it for you. To get started, could I just get your full name, please?

CUSTOMER: Owen Nguyen. That's O-W-E-N, Nguyen, N-G-U-Y-E-N.

AGENT: Thank you, Mr. Nguyen. And just to verify the account, can you please confirm the date of birth associated with the card?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Just give me one moment while my system pulls up your account details. It can be a little slow this afternoon.

CUSTOMER: Take your time.

AGENT: Okay… loading up here. So you’re in Denver, right? Rough game for the Lynx last night, huh?

CUSTOMER: Ugh, don’t remind me. I thought they had it in the third, but that last-minute fumble… painful. Just painful to watch. My son was devastated.

AGENT: I know, my whole family was yelling at the TV. At least the weather’s been nice. We’re finally getting some sun after all that rain.

CUSTOMER: That’s true. Can’t complain about that. Alright, is your, uh, system loaded?

AGENT: Yes, it is. Thank you for your patience. I see the account for Owen Nguyen with the Chase Ink Business Cash card. Which card are we talking about today? Is it the one ending in 3371?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s the one. Or, it *was*. I lost it. I think I left it at a restaurant last week, on Thursday. I called in and reported it lost right away using the automated phone thing.

AGENT: Okay, I see that. Let me check the notes here. Hmm. Yes, I'm seeing a record right here from... let's see... September 3rd. It says the card ending in 3371 was reported lost via the phone banking system.

CUSTOMER: Right. And the system said a new one was on its way. But since then, it’s been a total mess. I got an email that my Spotify subscription was declined. Then another for Adobe. These are business expenses, I need them. And then yesterday I tried to buy lunch using Google Pay on my phone, which is usually linked to that card, and it was declined too. What’s going on? Is the new card not active? Did I do something wrong?

AGENT: No, no, Mr. Nguyen, you did everything correctly. Let me explain what I'm seeing on my end. So, when you reported the card lost on the 3rd, the system immediately closed that card number—the one ending in 3371—to protect you from any fraudulent charges. That’s standard procedure.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that makes sense.

AGENT: At the same time, the system automatically issued a replacement card, which will have a new number. I see that was sent via standard mail, and the typical delivery time is five to seven business days.

CUSTOMER: Five to seven *business* days? So it might not even be here until the end of this week?

AGENT: That’s correct. Looking at the tracking, it currently shows as IN_TRANSIT, so it is on its way to the address we have on file for you in Denver.

CUSTOMER: But what about my payments? The Adobe one is for my whole design team. And the tap-to-pay? I thought that would just... you know, update.

AGENT: I understand your frustration, and I can see here exactly what happened. The recurring charges for Spotify and Adobe were declined because they were trying to bill the old, closed card number. The merchants haven't been provided with the new number yet. Once your new card arrives, you’ll need to log into those services and update your payment information with the new card number and expiration date.

CUSTOMER: Okay. So I just have to wait for the mail. And what about the phone payment? The Google Pay thing?

AGENT: Yes, I see that here as well. A declined tap-to-pay attempt. When the old card was closed, the digital wallet tokens associated with it were also revoked for security. So even though your phone’s wallet looks like it has the card, the link to the actual account was severed. You’ll need to add the new card to your Google Pay wallet once it arrives and you activate it.

CUSTOMER: So basically, I’m just stuck. I can't use my card or my phone for anything until a piece of plastic shows up in my mailbox. It’s a bit ridiculous. My wife, Renata, her business card is working fine, the one ending in 4969. But mine is the primary one we use for all the subscriptions.

AGENT: I do apologize for the inconvenience, Mr. Nguyen. I know it’s not ideal when you’re trying to run a business. The security measures are automatic to protect the account, but it does create this waiting period. There isn’t a way for me to reactivate the old card number or push the new card information to your digital wallet before the physical card arrives.

CUSTOMER: So… you can’t do anything? I waited on hold just to be told to wait some more?

AGENT: I can’t expedite the mail, but what I can do is open a case to have this situation formally documented and reviewed. This will create a record of the disruption to your services. And I can schedule a follow-up call with you to ensure that by a certain date, everything is resolved. How does that sound?

CUSTOMER: A case, okay. I guess that's something.

AGENT: Alright, I'm opening the case now. Just a moment… Okay. The reference number for this is CASE-9879276. And I can schedule a specialist to call you back to make sure you've received the card and that your digital wallet and recurring payments are getting sorted. The earliest I can book that is for September 10, 2026. Would that work for you? That should give enough time for the card to arrive.

CUSTOMER: September 10th… Yeah, fine. Let’s do that.

AGENT: Great. And what is the best number for us to reach you at for that callback?

CUSTOMER: Uh, just my office landline. It's 303-555-0309. Wait, no, sorry, I always mix that up. It's 303-555-0390.

AGENT: Okay, I have that down. A callback scheduled for September 10, 2026, to your office landline, 303-555-0390. And I'll note that it's a landline, not a mobile.

CUSTOMER: Good. Oh, hey, while I have you on the line, there was something else. I was looking at my last statement before all this happened, and there’s a charge I don't recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with a dispute. Do you have the details?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, hold on, I have the PDF open here. It was for… I think it was at Dollar General? No, that’s not it, that was the line above. Here it is. It says ‘Brightline Fitness Club’. For $669.35.

AGENT: Brightline Fitness Club. And the amount was six hundred sixty-nine dollars and thirty-five cents?

CUSTOMER: That’s it. And the location says Pittsburgh, PA. I’ve never even been to Pittsburgh. We’re in Denver. It makes no sense.

AGENT: I see. And you don’t recognize this charge at all? No one else authorized on the account would have made this purchase?

CUSTOMER: No, it's just me on this card. It's definitely not mine.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. I’m initiating a dispute for you now. Just to be clear for the record, you are disputing the charge of $669.35 from Brightline Fitness Club in Pittsburgh, PA. I'm filing this under our standard code for a charge from an unknown merchant, which is DISPUTE_RC_13.1.

CUSTOMER: Whatever the code is, as long as I don’t have to pay for someone else’s gym membership.

AGENT: Absolutely. The process is that we will issue a temporary credit for the amount while we investigate. The investigation can take some time, but we’ll contact the merchant and get to the bottom of it. You'll see the temporary credit on your account within one to two billing cycles. Just be aware that if a payment is late for any reason, it can incur a late fee of up to $39.00, so it's good you're addressing this now.

CUSTOMER: Right, okay.

AGENT: Your dispute reference number is DSP-2462284. You should also receive a letter in the mail outlining the next steps. And you know what, Mr. Nguyen, for all the trouble you’ve been through with the card replacement and the declined payments, I’d like to offer you a $30.00 courtesy credit for the inconvenience. I can apply that to your account right now.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thanks. I appreciate that.

AGENT: Of course. Just give me one second to process that for you... I'm just typing in the reason code here... and applying the credit... hmm. That's odd. Ah, it looks like… hmm. It looks like the system isn't letting me apply that credit right now, Mr. Nguyen. I'm very sorry, it seems you're not eligible at this time for a courtesy credit. I do apologize for offering that.

CUSTOMER: You’re kidding me. So you offer me something and then take it back? This whole call has been one thing after another.

AGENT: I am sincerely sorry about that. The system has final say, and I shouldn't have spoken too soon. I truly apologize for the frustration this has caused.

CUSTOMER: Unbelievable. Fine. Just… just make sure that dispute is filed and the callback is scheduled.

AGENT: I can absolutely confirm that for you. I have successfully filed dispute DSP-2462284 for the charge from Brightline Fitness Club. And I have you scheduled for a callback on September 10, 2026. The overall issue is being tracked under case number CASE-9879276. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No. No, that’s more than enough for one day. Thanks. I guess.

AGENT: I understand. Thank you again for calling Chase Business Card Services, Mr. Nguyen. I hope the rest of your day is better.

CUSTOMER: Yeah, you too. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

cust_synth_012:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Elena Mensah came in to the Westgate Commons branch around 2 PM today. It's been a pretty quiet Tuesday, so I was happy to have someone to chat with. She seemed a little flustered from the drive; she mentioned coming all the way from her place in Charlotte and that the traffic was worse than usual. I offered her a coffee from our new machine—the one that marketing insisted we install—and she was really impressed with it. Said it was much better than the old drip pot. We chatted for a bit about that and how surprisingly good the espresso setting is. She was very friendly and easy to talk to.

After the coffee small talk, we got down to business. She said she needed to make a payment on her credit card, her Chase Freedom Flex. She pulled out her card (*1765) for me to look up her account and a cashier's check from another institution. I pulled up her profile and confirmed her identity with her driver's license. Everything looked standard. The check was for a fairly large amount, so I prepped the payment screen. I took the check from her and started keying in the details. My fingers must have been moving faster than my brain because I typed in `$2,500.00` initially. It's an easy mistake to make, a 5 instead of a 0. Luckily, I have a habit of always double-checking the physical check against the screen before I hit submit. I saw the mismatch right away and let out a little "oops." I told her I'd almost given us a little extra, and corrected the amount on my screen to the proper `$2,050.00`. She laughed and said she wouldn't have complained. I confirmed the corrected amount with her one more time and then processed the transaction.

This is where things got a little bit awkward. Since it was a cashier's check, I initially told her it would be great because the payment should have `same-day availability`. I've seen that happen before and just spoke a little too soon. As soon as I submitted the payment, the system flagged it and applied a standard hold on the funds. A big notification popped up on my screen. I had to backtrack and apologize to Ms. Mensah, explaining that my initial statement was incorrect and that the system had automatically placed a hold on the payment. I showed her the screen and explained that it's standard procedure for cashier's check payments on a credit card account, to ensure the funds clear properly. I explained that for really large amounts, like anything over `$5,000.00`, the hold can sometimes be even longer, but hers fell under our standard policy. She was a little disappointed but very understanding, which I appreciated. It's always embarrassing when you have to correct yourself like that. I confirmed the hold details for her and let her know the funds would be fully applied and the hold would be released on `June 14, 2026`. I printed out her receipt, made sure to highlight the payment amount and the funds availability date, and handed it to her. The receipt number for her records is `BRC-4796190`.

Once that was all settled, she had another question. She asked if she could also make a payment on her partner Jordan's card. She had the card number, or at least the last few digits, which she said ended in `5695`. I had to explain that unfortunately, due to privacy and security policies, I couldn't process a payment for a cardholder who wasn't present to authorize it. I told her Jordan would need to come into a branch themselves with ID, or they could make a payment through their own online banking portal or our mobile app. She nodded and said she figured as much but thought it was worth asking since she was already here.

As she was putting her wallet away, I noticed a sticker on it for the Lakeside Lynx. I'm a huge fan, so I asked her about it. Her whole demeanor lit up and we spent the next five or ten minutes talking about their season. She was at the last home game and was telling me all about the energy in the stadium. We both agreed that their new forward is going to be a game-changer if he can stay healthy. It was a really nice way to end the interaction, especially after the slight hiccup with the funds hold. It totally smoothed things over. She thanked me for my help and for the coffee, and I wished her a safe drive back to Charlotte. I think she left feeling good about the visit, which is always the goal.

Follow-up:
No follow-up action is required. Customer made a payment of `$2,050.00` toward her Chase Freedom Flex (*1765) via cashier's check. Receipt `BRC-4796190` was provided. Customer was informed of the funds hold until `June 14, 2026` and was understanding. Also advised on policy for making payments for a third party (her partner's card ending in `5695`). The interaction ended positively.

cust_synth_012:LM1_CALL.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en Español, oprima dos. For all other languages, press three.
Please listen carefully as our menu options have recently changed.
For lost or stolen cards, or to report suspicious activity, press one.
To check your account balance or recent transactions, press two.
For information on new products or to apply for a new card, press three.
To speak to a representative, please stay on the line.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account, check your balance, and pay your bill anytime in the Chase mobile app? Download it today from your phone’s app store.
(music plays)
Apply for the Chase Freedom Flex card today and earn a $200.00 statement credit after you spend five hundred dollars on purchases in your first three months from account opening. Plus, earn five percent cash back on bonus categories each quarter you activate. Terms apply.
(music plays)
Your call is important to us. A representative will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, you're through to Chase. My name is David. Who am I speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, my name is Elena Mensah.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Mensah. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Well, I’m hoping you can. I am having a bit of a nightmare. I lost my card a few days ago, I called the automated line and reported it, and I was told a new one was on the way. But I still don't have it, and now things are getting declined, my gym membership, my Peloton... I tried to use my watch to pay for lunch yesterday and that didn't work either. It's just a mess.

AGENT: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that, Ms. Mensah. That sounds incredibly frustrating. I can definitely look into that for you. To pull up your account, I just need to verify a few details for security. Can you please confirm your date of birth for me?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s…

AGENT: Thank you. Perfect. And just one moment while I get your profile loaded up here. Sometimes the system can be a little slow on a Monday morning.

CUSTOMER: I know the feeling.

AGENT: How's the weather down in Charlotte today? A bit nicer than it is up here, I imagine.

CUSTOMER: It's actually beautiful, finally cooling off a little bit. We’re all just recovering from the Miners game on Saturday. What a disaster.

AGENT: Oh, don't tell me about it. My brother-in-law had tickets, he was just miserable. I think they need to rethink their entire defense.

CUSTOMER: You and the rest of the state. It was just embarrassing.

AGENT: Right? Okay, looks like I have your account here now. So, I'm just taking a look at the notes... Okay. I can see your Chase Freedom Flex card... the one ending in one-seven-six-five. Is that the card you reported lost?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s the one.

AGENT: Okay. And I do see that on... let me see the date... Saturday, September 12th, it was reported lost through our automated phone system. Is that correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s right. I couldn’t find it after I got home from errands. I was in a bit of a panic.

AGENT: Of course, that's completely understandable. Well, you did exactly the right thing. So, what happens is, as soon as you reported it, the system immediately closed that card to protect you from any fraudulent charges. That's status `CARD_CLOSED_LOST` on my screen.

CUSTOMER: Okay, so that’s why my gym membership was declined? I got an email from them.

AGENT: That’s exactly it. I see notes here that on the 13th, there were two attempted recurring charges—one from Peloton and one from Planet Fitness—that were declined because they were trying to bill that closed card number.

CUSTOMER: So what do I do? Do I have to call them all and give them the new number?

AGENT: Yes, once you receive and activate your new card, you'll need to update your payment information with any merchants who bill you automatically. We can't do that for them, unfortunately.

CUSTOMER: Okay. And what about my watch? I tried to use my Garmin watch to pay and it just said 'declined'. It was so embarrassing.

AGENT: Right, I see that here as well. A tap-to-pay decline at a place called Nobu. So, when the physical card was closed, the system also automatically revoked the digital wallet token that was connected to it. It’s another security measure. Your watch was essentially trying to use a digital key for a lock we’d already changed.

CUSTOMER: This is so complicated. So when am I actually going to get this new card? I feel like I'm completely stuck. My partner Jordan's card works fine, thank god, the one ending in 2393, or we wouldn't be able to buy groceries.

AGENT: I completely understand your frustration, Ms. Mensah. Let me check the delivery status for you. Okay... I see the replacement card, a new Chase Freedom Flex ending in... three-four-one-five, was issued on the 12th and sent out via standard mail. The tracking just says `IN_TRANSIT`. Standard delivery is five to seven business days, so... let's see, it was sent on the 12th, which was a Saturday... so it really should be arriving any day now. Sometimes it can take the full seven business days.

CUSTOMER: So there's nothing you can do to speed it up?

AGENT: I'm afraid not on this call, as it's already in the mail system. However, what I am going to do is open a formal case for this. This creates a record of our conversation and escalates it so that if the card doesn't arrive in, say, the next two days, we have a team that can immediately investigate and, if needed, expedite a new one via courier. Does that sound okay?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I suppose so. At least it's something.

AGENT: Okay, I am opening that for you right now. It's just loading... Okay. The reference number for this case is `CASE-8056913`. I'd recommend just jotting that down.

CUSTOMER: Okay, `CASE-8056913`. Got it.

AGENT: Perfect. And to make sure this is resolved for you, I'd also like to schedule a callback with a specialist. They'll be able to see the full picture and take further action if the card is still missing. I can book that for, let’s see… how about `September 20, 2026`? That gives the mail a few more days.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that works.

AGENT: Great. And what is the best number for us to reach you at for that callback?

CUSTOMER: Uh, you can call my office landline. It's `704-555-0441`... oh, wait, sorry, I always do that. It's `704-555-0414`.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me just read that back to you. That's a callback scheduled for September 20th, 2026, to the number `704-555-0414`. And I see that's an office landline you're giving me, so I'll just note that we are not changing the mobile number we have on file for you.

CUSTOMER: That’s right. Thank you. Oh, actually, while I have you... I was looking at my last statement online, before the card got lost, and there's a charge on there I don't recognize at all.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly help you with that. Do you have the details there?

CUSTOMER: I think so, let me pull it up again. I thought it was at `Big Lots` at first, but that wasn't it... hold on... okay, here it is. It says `Lakeview Pet Grooming`. For `$165.64`.

AGENT: Okay, `Lakeview Pet Grooming`, one hundred sixty-five dollars and sixty-four cents. And can you see the location of that merchant?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it says `Raleigh, NC`. I've never even been to `Raleigh, NC`. I don't have a pet that needs grooming, for that matter.

AGENT: I see. Thank you for clarifying that. Just one moment while I open up our dispute tool. Okay. So, to file this dispute, I just need to read you a quick disclosure. The dispute process can take up to two billing cycles to be fully resolved. We will issue a temporary credit for the amount of `$165.64` to your account while we investigate. If the charge is found to be valid, the credit will be reversed. Do you understand and wish to proceed?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I do.

AGENT: Thank you. And just as a general reminder for all customers, any payments not received by the due date may result in a late fee of up to `$41.00`. That's just a standard disclosure I have to read while the system processes. Okay... and I am filing this now. The reason code I am using is `DISPUTE_RC_13.3`, which corresponds to "Cardholder states transaction took place in a city they were not in". It's all submitted. Your reference number for this dispute is `DSP-6272547`.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that’s a lot of numbers. `DSP-6272547`. Got it.

AGENT: Excellent. Ms. Mensah, I know this has been a really trying experience, and I do sincerely apologize for all the trouble with the card delivery and the declined payments. To thank you for your patience today, I'm going to go ahead and apply `a $15.00` courtesy credit to your account. It should appear within one to two business days. Let me just process that for you now... hmm.

CUSTOMER: What's wrong?

AGENT: Oh, for goodness sake. I am so sorry. It looks like the system is rejecting the credit. It seems that because the new card isn't activated yet, my tool to post credits is locked out. That is my fault, I should have anticipated that.

CUSTOMER: You have got to be kidding me.

AGENT: I know, and I am truly sorry. I will add a detailed note to the case file, that's `CASE-8056913`, and I will instruct the agent who calls you back on the 20th to apply that credit for you first thing. They will be able to do it once your new card is active.

CUSTOMER: Fine. Just... fine. As long as someone does it.

AGENT: They will. I've made it the primary action on the case. So, just to recap: we've documented the issue with your replacement card under case number `CASE-8056913`; we have a callback scheduled for you on `September 20, 2026` to `704-555-0414`; and we have filed a dispute for the `$165.64` charge from `Lakeview Pet Grooming` under reference `DSP-6272547`. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, I think that’s more than enough for one day. I’ll just wait for the card and the call.

AGENT: I understand. Thank you again for your patience, Ms. Mensah. I hope the card arrives tomorrow. Thank you for calling Chase, and have a good rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.

cust_synth_014:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Marcus Costa came into the Riverbend Plaza branch this afternoon, maybe around two o'clock. I recognized him right away, he's been in a few times before and he's always very pleasant. He was grabbing a cup of coffee from our new machine in the lobby, and I asked him how he liked it. He said it was a huge improvement over the old one, which I had to agree with. The old one made a noise like a dying sea lion and the coffee tasted like it had been filtered through a sock. This new one is much quieter and actually makes a decent cup. He mentioned his commute in from Portland was surprisingly smooth today, which is always a good start to the day.

We got to chatting for a minute about the Riverdale Rovers. I was wearing my Rovers pin on my lanyard and he noticed it. He's a big fan, too. We talked about that tough loss last weekend and how frustrating it was, but he's still really optimistic about their chances this season. I am too, honestly. If they can just get their defense sorted out, I think they have a real shot at the playoffs. It’s nice to connect with a customer like that, makes the day go by faster.

Anyway, after the sports talk, we got down to business. Marcus said he needed to make a large payment on his credit card. He pulled out his Amazon Prime Visa (*3270) and a cashier's check from another institution. He handed the check over to me and I began the payment process in the system. I was probably still thinking about the Rovers' questionable penalty kick when I was keying in the numbers. I glanced at the check, saw the "4" and the "2" and my fingers just sort of flew across the keypad. I keyed in the payment as $4,200.00. I even said it out loud, "Okay, Marcus, we're processing a payment of four thousand two hundred dollars to your Visa card."

As the system was thinking, I double-checked the physical check in my hand, just as a matter of procedure to verify the payee name was correct. That's when I saw it. The amount was clearly written as $4,020.00, not what I had typed. My brain just filled in the zero. I felt my face get a little warm. "Oh, you know what, hold on a second," I said. "My apologies, my fingers got ahead of me there. The amount is actually four thousand and twenty dollars, not four thousand two hundred. Let me cancel this and re-enter it correctly." He was very gracious about it, just laughed and said "no problem, happens to the best of us." I cancelled the initial entry and carefully re-keyed the correct amount, $4,020.00. I confirmed with him one more time, "Okay, for real this time, a payment of four thousand and twenty dollars. That's correct, right?" He nodded.

I submitted the corrected payment. As it was processing, I told him, "Since you're using a cashier's check, this should be as good as cash, so you'll see same-day availability on your card's available credit." Famous last words. Of course, as soon as I said that, the system screen refreshed with a big notification: "Standard Funds Hold Applied." I should have known. Our system automatically holds almost all cashier's checks for a few days for verification, it's been the policy for years. I had to backtrack for the second time in five minutes.

"Actually, Marcus, I have to apologize again, the system has a mind of its own today," I said, trying to keep it light. "It looks like it did place a standard hold on the funds. It's a default security measure for this type of payment, I completely misspoke about it being available immediately." I then explained that it’s just a blanket policy. I mentioned that for very large checks, say, anything over $7,500.00, the hold can sometimes be even longer, but his was well under that threshold so it would just be the standard hold period. He didn't seem bothered, just asked when the payment would actually go through. I clicked into the hold details on my screen and found the specific date. "It says right here the hold will be released on April 28, 2026. So the payment will be fully posted and reflected on that date." I printed out his receipt and handed it to him. "And here is your receipt for the transaction. The reference number for your records is BRC-1042936."

Just as he was putting the receipt in his wallet and getting ready to leave, he paused. He asked if he could also make a payment for his partner, Casey. He said he thought their card number ended in 6926. I had to explain our privacy policy, that because Casey wasn't here to authorize the transaction on their own account, I couldn't accept a payment from him on their behalf. I explained that Casey would need to come into a branch personally, or they could always make a payment themselves through the mobile app or our website. He was totally understanding about it, said he figured as much but thought he'd ask while he was here. We wrapped up with a final "Go Rovers!" and he headed out. A really nice guy, very patient with my fumbles today.

Follow-up:
None required. Customer was satisfied with the explanation regarding the funds hold and the policy for third-party payments. No further action needed.

cust_synth_015:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Nadia Kaplan came into the Mill Creek Crossing branch this afternoon, around 2 PM. I remember her from a few months ago, so it was nice to see a familiar face. She was commenting on our new coffee machine, asked if it was any good. I told her it's a huge improvement and offered her a cup, but she said she was on her way to a meeting and already over-caffeinated from her morning commute. We chatted for a minute about the traffic getting out of the city; she lives in Philadelphia but apparently works out here a few days a week. It sounds like a rough drive.

She got down to business and said she needed to make a large payment on her Chase Sapphire Preferred card. I pulled up her profile and confirmed her identity with her driver's license. Everything looked standard. She handed me a cashier's check. I took a look at it and she mentioned she’d just sold some old furniture and wanted to put the whole amount toward her balance before the next statement date. Smart move. I started processing the payment, keying in the details. I must have been distracted by the conversation or just had a bit of a brain-fade, because I initially typed in the payment amount as $2,450.00. I was just about to hit the final confirmation when I glanced back at the physical check in my hand and saw the numbers didn't match. Whoops. It's a good thing we have that final review screen.

I immediately corrected the entry on my screen to the proper amount of $2,540.00, making sure it matched the cashier's check exactly this time. I apologized to Nadia and just made a little joke about needing that coffee after all. She was very understanding about it, laughed and said it happens. Once the amount was corrected, I told her that using a cashier's check was a good choice as it meant she would get same-day availability for the payment credit. I processed the payment and the system generated the receipt. The receipt number is BRC-1014218.

However, as the receipt was printing, a notification popped up on my terminal that a hold was being placed on the funds. This was embarrassing as I had just told her the opposite. I had to immediately walk back my statement about same-day availability. I explained that I was mistaken and that while that's often the case, the system had automatically placed a standard hold on this specific transaction. I showed her on the screen that the funds from the cashier's check would not be fully available to her credit line until the hold releases on June 27, 2026. She was a little confused and asked why, since it was a cashier's check and not a personal one. I explained that it's a standard security procedure for certain types of non-cash payments, and that even cashier's checks over a certain threshold, like $7,500.00, can sometimes be held for even longer periods. She wasn't thrilled, but she understood it was a system policy and not something I could override at the branch level. I made sure to point out the hold release date on her copy of the receipt.

While I was stapling her receipt to a copy of the transaction record, she asked if she could also make a payment for her wife, Renata. She said her wife's card ends in 4775 and she had the card number written down. I had to explain that unfortunately, for privacy and security reasons, I couldn't process a payment on an account for someone who wasn't present to authorize it. I let her know that Renata would need to come in person, or she could easily make the payment herself through the mobile app or online banking. Nadia said she understood and would just tell her wife to do it online later.

To lighten the mood after the back-and-forth about the hold, I noticed she was wearing a Granite Falls Miners cap. I asked her if she was a fan and if she thought they had a chance of making the playoffs this year. That got her talking. Turns out she's a huge fan, goes to a few games a season. We spent a couple of minutes debating their new pitcher and whether the manager made the right call in the last game. She said being from Philadelphia, she has high standards for sports teams, but the Miners are starting to win her over. It was a good way to end the interaction on a positive note. I walked her to the door, thanked her for coming in, and wished her a better commute home.

Follow-up:
- No immediate follow-up required from my side.
- Payment of $2,540.00 was successfully processed to the customer's Chase Sapphire Preferred (*2016) via cashier's check.
- Customer was provided with receipt BRC-1014218.
- Customer was made aware of the funds hold and its release date of June 27, 2026.
- Advised customer that her wife would need to be present to make a payment on her own card account. No action was taken on card ending 4775.

cust_synth_017:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Mr. Andre Haddad came into the Mill Creek Crossing branch this afternoon, around 2 PM. He seemed a little frazzled from the traffic, mentioned he was just passing through on his way back home to Atlanta and the GPS had routed him onto some crazy back roads. I offered him a coffee from our new machine but he politely declined, said he was already caffeinated enough for one day. He had his Chase Slate Edge card (*4628) in hand and said he needed to make a fairly large payment on the balance.

He presented a cashier's check. I took it and began the payment process in the system. While I was keying everything in, we chatted for a bit. He saw the Lakeside Lynx poster we have up behind the teller line and asked if I was a fan. I told him I was a huge fan, born and raised around here, and we spent a few minutes talking about their disappointing end to the season. He agreed they really need to find a more consistent defense if they want to make a serious run next year. He was really knowledgeable, a genuine fan. It's always nice when you can connect with a customer like that. He said he tries to catch a game whenever he's in town for work.

Anyway, while we were talking about the Lynx, I must have gotten distracted. I entered the payment amount and was about to hit submit when I did my standard double-check against the physical check. My heart kind of sank for a second. I had keyed in the payment as $3,070.00. A classic finger fumble. Thankfully I caught it before processing. I laughed and told him, "Whoops, looks like I need that coffee after all," and showed him the screen so he could see I was correcting it. I voided the initial entry and re-keyed the correct payment amount of $3,700.00, carefully verifying it against the check a second and third time. He was very understanding about it.

After I processed the corrected payment, I initially told him that because he was making the payment in-branch before the daily cutoff, he should see same-day availability for the credit on his account. However, as the transaction finalized, the system automatically placed a hold on the funds. I had a moment of "oh, of course" – it's a cashier's check, not cash or a direct transfer. I had to immediately walk back what I just said, which is always embarrassing. I apologized and explained that my initial comment was for cash payments and that for cashier's checks, there's a standard hold while the funds are formally verified. He was patient but I could tell he was a little disappointed. I pulled up the hold details and showed him on my monitor that the funds from the $3,700.00 payment would be fully available and credited to his Chase Slate Edge account on March 13, 2026. I reiterated the date, March 13, 2026, to make sure it was clear. I explained it's a system-wide policy for security and to protect both him and the bank, and that for very large checks, say over $10,000.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer. He seemed to understand once I framed it that way. I printed his receipt, confirmed the receipt number BRC-8343175 with him, and highlighted the payment amount and hold release date for his records.

Just as he was about to leave, he hesitated and asked a question on behalf of his partner, Jordan. He asked if he could also make a payment on Jordan’s card, and he had the last four digits, 5496. I had to explain that for privacy and security reasons, I couldn't access an account or process a payment for anyone who isn't the account holder and isn't present with a valid ID. I told him Jordan would either need to come into a branch personally, or they could easily make a payment through the online portal or our mobile app. He nodded, said he figured as much but thought he'd ask while he was here. He thanked me for my help and for the chat about the Lakeside Lynx.

Overall a pretty standard interaction, aside from my own fumble with the amount and then misstating the availability. Mr. Haddad was pleasant and patient throughout, even with the small hiccups.

Follow-up:
No follow-up action required from my side. Payment of $3,700.00 is processing and subject to a standard funds hold until March 13, 2026. Will make a mental note to be more careful quoting availability times for non-cash payments to avoid confusion in the future. Customer was informed of all details and left with receipt BRC-8343175.

cust_synth_018:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Mei Abara came in around 2:30 PM, just after the mid-afternoon rush had finally died down. She's not a regular at the Westgate Commons branch, I don't think I've seen her before. She was pleasant, a little hurried. Said the traffic getting here from her office was a nightmare. I offered her a coffee from the new machine, telling her it’s a huge step up from the old one, but she politely declined, just wanted to get this errand done and get back on the road. She mentioned she's from Philadelphia originally and that the drivers here are a whole different breed. I had to agree with her on that.

She pulled out her Chase Sapphire Preferred card and a cashier's check, and wanted to make a big payment toward the balance. I confirmed her identity with her driver's license and pulled up her account for the card ending in *6057. She was chatting a bit while I was getting everything set up, saw the Riverdale Rovers sticker on her water bottle. I asked if she was a fan and her face lit up. We spent a good five minutes talking about the last game and how we both think the new striker is exactly what the team needed. She’s optimistic about the rest of the season, which is nice to hear. I’m a bit more of a pessimist after the last few years, but I kept that to myself. It’s just nice to connect with a customer over something other than account fees.

Anyway, back to business. I took the cashier’s check from her and started keying in the payment. I was still half-thinking about the Rovers' chances on Saturday when I typed it in. "Okay, Ms. Abara, so that's a payment of $4,400.00 going toward your Sapphire Preferred balance," I said, reading from my screen. She looked at me, a little confused, and I immediately realized I should check the paper again. Sure enough, my fingers had gotten ahead of my brain. "Oh, you know what, I am so sorry," I said, laughing a little. "My kingdom for a 'go back' button on this keyboard. The check is clearly for $4,040.00. Let me correct that right now. That's what I get for trying to multitask and think about soccer." I voided the initial entry and re-keyed the payment for the correct amount, $4,040.00, reading it back to her carefully this time and showing her the screen to confirm.

I told her, "Alright, since you're using a cashier's check, that should post with same-day availability for your available credit." And then, of course, the system proved me a liar. As soon as I hit 'submit,' a little yellow flag popped up on the transaction. A funds hold. Of course. I had to backtrack immediately. "Actually, Ms. Abara, I need to apologize again, I spoke too soon. It looks like the system has automatically placed a standard hold on this payment because it's a cashier's check from another institution. I am very sorry for the misinformation." She was understanding, but you could tell she was a bit disappointed. I explained that it's a mandatory verification period to ensure the funds clear properly. I double-checked the hold details on my screen and told her, "I can see here that the hold is set to be released on April 30, 2026. The payment will be fully credited and finalized on that date." I also explained that this is standard procedure for this type of payment and that for cashier's checks over $5,000.00, the hold can sometimes be even longer. She seemed to appreciate the context. I printed out the receipt for her, which shows the payment amount of $4,040.00, and made sure to highlight the receipt number, BRC-9575907, for her records.

Just as I thought we were done, she asked if she could also make a payment for her partner, Jordan. She said their card ends in 2856 and she had the account number, but not the physical card. I had to explain our privacy and security policy, that I couldn't accept a payment or even look up an account for someone who wasn't present to provide ID. I told her that Jordan would need to come into a branch personally, or they could make the payment themselves through the mobile app or online banking. She understood completely, said it made sense, but that it was worth a shot to ask while she was here.

We ended the visit on a good note, circling back to the Riverdale Rovers. I wished her team luck, and she said she'd be back on the road, hopefully to make it home before the evening rush really kicked in. She was perfectly nice about the whole thing, especially my little slip-ups with the amount and the hold information. It just goes to show you should never promise anything until the system gives you the final say.

Follow-up:
No immediate action needed. Customer has receipt BRC-9575907 and was advised of the funds hold releasing on April 30, 2026. She understood the policy regarding making payments on behalf of her partner (for card ending 2856) and was not upset. Just a note to be more careful quoting availability on cashier's check payments in the future.

cust_synth_020:LM1_CALL.body:
IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en español, oprima dos. For card services, press one. For loans and mortgages, press two. To report a card lost or stolen, press three. For all other inquiries, or to speak to a representative, press four.
IVR: Please be aware that calls may be recorded for quality and training purposes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn 60,000 bonus points with the Chase Sapphire Preferred card after you spend four thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening? That's seven hundred and fifty dollars toward travel when you redeem through Chase Ultimate Rewards. Ask your representative for more details. An agent will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. My name is David, and you've reached Card Services. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, hello. I’m having a problem with my credit card. My Chase Freedom Unlimited. It just... stopped working. I think it expired? And I got a new one in the mail but I can't get it to activate.

AGENT: Okay, I can definitely look into that for you. I'm sorry to hear you're having trouble. To pull up your account, could I please get your full name and date of birth?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's Mei Ferreira.

AGENT: Thank you, Ms. Ferreira. And the date of birth?

CUSTOMER: It's [Date of Birth].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you for that. Just give my system a moment to load your profile here. It can be a little slow on a Monday morning.

CUSTOMER: No problem.

AGENT: So you're in Atlanta, I see. How's the weather down there today?

CUSTOMER: Oh, it's hot. Humid. You know, just another September day here. My air conditioning is working overtime.

AGENT: I can imagine. It’s actually starting to get a little chilly up here. Anyway, did you happen to catch that Granite Falls Miners game last night? I’m still recovering.

CUSTOMER: Ugh, don't even talk about it. My husband was about to throw the remote through the television screen. I can't believe they blew that lead in the fourth. Just a total disaster.

AGENT: Tell me about it. I almost turned it off. Okay, looks like I have your file open now. Thanks for your patience. So, let’s see what's going on with that card.

CUSTOMER: Thank you. Yeah, I tried to buy gas and it was declined, and an online order, too. Then I realized the card said it expired at the end of August.

AGENT: Yes, okay, I see it all here. So your Chase Freedom Unlimited card, the one ending in five-zero-one-nine, did indeed expire at the end of last month. That's why I'm seeing a couple of declined transactions on September sixth. One at BP Fuel Stop and one at Best Buy Online.

CUSTOMER: Right, that was me. So I got out the new one you guys sent, but when I went into the app to activate it, it just... it wouldn't work. It said it sent a code to my phone, but I never received anything.

AGENT: Okay, that is the key piece of information. I see the replacement card was mailed out in mid-August. That’s the one ending in six-three-four-six, is that the one you have?

CUSTOMER: Yes, six-three-four-six. That's it. It’s useless right now.

AGENT: Right. So, I am looking at the system log here, and I can see an activation attempt was made from the mobile app on September sixth. At that point, as a security measure, the system sent a one-time passcode to the mobile number we have on file for verification purposes. The number it sent that code to ends in the digits one-three-one-eight. Does that phone number sound familiar at all?

CUSTOMER: Oh, for crying out loud. No. That's my old number. I haven't had that number in at least two years. I can't believe that's still in your system somewhere. I updated it on the website.

AGENT: I understand your frustration, Ms. Ferreira, and I see your primary contact number is correct. It appears this specific field, the one used for two-factor authentication on card activations, was not updated at the same time. It's a separate security profile. Because that code was sent to the wrong number and it timed out, the activation failed.

CUSTOMER: So I'm stuck with a card that doesn't work because of a number I don't have anymore. This is ridiculous. My sister Yuki's card, the one ending 9351, she never has these problems. Can you just activate it for me now, over the phone? Or at least update that number so I can do it myself?

AGENT: I wish it were that simple, and I truly apologize for the complexity here. Unfortunately, because the automated security verification has failed, a lock has been placed on the card's activation profile. It's a fraud prevention measure, and from my console, I don't have the ability to override it manually or change that verification number directly.

CUSTOMER: You have got to be kidding me. So you're telling me you can't help me? I have a piece of plastic here and I can't use it, and you, the bank, can't turn it on?

AGENT: I can absolutely help you get this resolved, it just requires an extra step. What I need to do is open a formal case for our back-office support team. They have higher-level permissions to securely verify your identity through other means, fix that contact detail in the security profile, and then unlock the card for activation. I'm so sorry for the runaround. I’m starting that case for you right now... just need to type in the details. One moment.

CUSTOMER: (Sighs) Fine. Whatever it takes.

AGENT: Okay, I have created the request. The case reference number is CASE-1783198. I would recommend writing that down.

CUSTOMER: Hang on, let me get a pen. Okay, what was it again?

AGENT: It's CASE-1783198.

CUSTOMER: Got it. So what happens now? Do I just wait?

AGENT: The team will review the case within two to three business days. Once they have unlocked your profile, we will need to call you back to complete the final activation step. I can schedule that callback for you now. What date and time would be best?

CUSTOMER: Um... I don't know. How about later this week? Thursday?

AGENT: Thursday is September 12, 2026. That works. Do you prefer morning or afternoon?

CUSTOMER: Afternoon would be better.

AGENT: Okay, I will book the callback for September 12, 2026, in a window between 2 PM and 4 PM Eastern Time. And what is the best number to reach you at for that call?

CUSTOMER: Please use my office landline. It’s a direct line. The number is 404-555-0219, sorry, 404-555-0291. My brain is fried today.

AGENT: Not a problem at all, I completely understand. Let me just confirm that. A callback to you on September 12, 2026, between 2 and 4 PM Eastern, at the phone number 404-555-0291. Is that all correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, 404-555-0291. That's the one.

AGENT: Perfect. I've noted that all in the case file. Again, Ms. Ferreira, I am very sorry for this whole mess. As a small apology for the inconvenience, I'd like to post a $15.00 courtesy credit to your account. Let me just process that... one moment... clicking through the screens here... hmm.

CUSTOMER: What now?

AGENT: Oh, you won't believe this. I am so sorry. It appears the system is rejecting the credit because the primary card on the account is in this suspended, non-activated state. It won't let me post any manual adjustments. I will add a strong note to CASE-1783198 for the next agent to apply that credit for you as soon as the card is active.

CUSTOMER: (Sighs heavily) Of course it is. Okay. Fine.

AGENT: I am truly sorry about that. Was there anything else I could assist with while I have you on the line?

CUSTOMER: Actually... yes. Since I'm stuck dealing with this, I was looking at my last statement online and I saw a charge I am positive isn't mine. Can you look at that?

AGENT: But of course. I can certainly help you with that. Which charge is it?

CUSTOMER: Let me pull it up again... It was on August 28th. The amount is $329.51. The merchant... I think it was at Burlington? No, that's not right, that was me. Hold on... okay, here. It says the name is Crescent Moon Bookshop.

AGENT: Okay, I see that transaction on your statement. August 28th for $329.51 at Crescent Moon Bookshop. And the location is listed as Boise, ID.

CUSTOMER: Exactly! Boise, ID. I've never been to Idaho in my life. I was in Atlanta that day, I was at work. That charge is not mine.

AGENT: Understood. And just to confirm, you didn't authorize anyone else, like a family member, to use your card for that purchase?

CUSTOMER: No, absolutely not.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. I am going to file a transaction dispute for you right now. It takes a few minutes to go through the process on my end. While I do this, I am required to read you a standard disclosure. Please be aware that if a payment is not made on time, it can result in a late fee of up to $40.00.

CUSTOMER: Right, but I always pay my bill on time. That's not an issue.

AGENT: I see that, Ms. Ferreira. It's just a required script. Okay... entering the details now... merchant name... amount... transaction date... and the reason for the dispute. Okay, that has been submitted. The dispute reference number is DSP-8431042.

CUSTOMER: Wow, that's a long one. Can you repeat it?

AGENT: Certainly. It's D, as in David, S, as in Sam, P, as in Paul, dash, 8-4-3-1-0-4-2.

CUSTOMER: DSP-8431042. Got it.

AGENT: I have filed it under the reason code DISPUTE_RC_12.6, which is for a transaction not recognized by the cardholder. Our investigation team will look into it. In the meantime, you should see a provisional credit for the full amount of $329.51 post to your account within one to two business days. You'll also receive some communication by mail regarding the dispute in the next week or so.

CUSTOMER: Okay, great. Well, at least we solved something today.

AGENT: Absolutely. So, to quickly recap our call, I've opened CASE-1783198 to get that new card activation issue resolved, with a callback scheduled to you for the afternoon of September 12, 2026, at your office number, 404-555-0291. And we have also filed dispute DSP-8431042 for that charge from Crescent Moon Bookshop. Was there anything else at all I could help with?

CUSTOMER: No, that is plenty for one day. Thank you for your help, David.

AGENT: You are most welcome, Ms. Ferreira. It was my pleasure to assist, and again, my sincere apologies for the trouble with the card activation. We'll get it sorted for you. Thank you for calling Chase, and please have a wonderful rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye now.

AGENT: Goodbye.

cust_synth_021:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Hannah Costa came into the Westgate Commons branch this afternoon, around 2 PM. She's not one of our regulars; her home address is in Charlotte, but she said she was in the area for a meeting and wanted to make a large payment in person rather than mailing a check. We chatted for a minute about her commute, which sounded awful, and I offered her a coffee from our new machine. She was very impressed with it, said it was much better than the old pot we used to have, which is true. She had her Chase Freedom Flex card with her and her driver's license, so I pulled up her profile after completing the standard verification.

Her goal was straightforward: make a payment on her Chase Freedom Flex (*4033) using a cashier's check she brought with her. She handed me the check and we were talking about the Lakeside Lynx and whether they have any chance of making the playoffs this year. I'm not optimistic but she was, and while we were talking I keyed in the payment. I think my fingers got ahead of my brain because I typed in `$1,960.00` initially. I was about to hit 'submit' when my screen flashed the amount and I glanced down at the physical check on my desk to do my mandatory double-check and saw the numbers didn't match. Whoops. The check was clearly for $1,690.00. I apologized and told her I must need another cup of coffee from that new machine, and she laughed. I voided the initial entry before it was fully processed and re-keyed the payment for the correct amount of $1,690.00. I showed her the screen this time to confirm the amount was correct before proceeding, which she appreciated.

I told her that because it was a cashier's check, she should see same-day availability for the payment, which is usually the case. However, when I submitted the corrected transaction, the system automatically placed a hold on the funds. The processing screen clearly flagged it. I had to immediately walk back my previous statement, which is always a bit awkward. I explained that I had spoken too soon and that for certain check types and amounts, even official checks, the system will sometimes apply a standard hold for verification. I explained it's a security measure to protect both her and the bank, and that it's completely automated. To provide some context, I mentioned that for cashier's checks over $5,000.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer, so this was just a standard, precautionary hold. She was a little disappointed but understood. I printed out the receipt for her and pointed to the specific details. The receipt number is BRC-9768573. I also showed her where it explicitly states the funds will be on hold and that the payment will be fully cleared and reflected in her available credit on June 15, 2026.

After we sorted that out, and she seemed okay with the situation, she mentioned she had one other question. She asked if she could also make a payment for her wife, Leonie. She didn't have the check for it, but wanted to know for next time what the process was. She said the card ends in 5010. I explained that due to privacy and security policies, we can't accept a payment from her on an account that is not in her name. I let her know that Leonie would either need to come into a branch herself with her ID, or she could make a payment anytime through the mobile app, online, or over the phone. I clarified that I couldn't even look up the account for her. She understood completely, said that's what she figured but wanted to ask just in case. We finished up our chat about the Lakeside Lynx (she's still more optimistic than I am) and she thanked me for the help. She was very pleasant throughout the whole visit, even with my typing mistake and the mix-up on the funds availability.

Follow-up:
No immediate follow-up required with the customer. I have set a personal reminder to check on the payment to the Chase Freedom Flex (*4033) on or around June 15, 2026, just to ensure the hold releases automatically as the system indicated. Customer was informed about policy regarding payments on third-party accounts (re: card ending 5010) and no action was taken.

AGENT: Of course. I can certainly help with that.

CUSTOMER: No. Never heard of them. And it says the location is Tucson, AZ. I’ve never been to Tucson in my life. We haven't bought any furniture. It’s definitely not mine.

AGENT: You are very welcome, Ms. Costa. I hope the rest of your day is much smoother. And, go Miners! Hopefully.

AGENT: Goodbye.

cust_synth_022:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Aisha Abara came into the Riverbend Plaza branch this afternoon, around two o'clock. She's not one of our regulars, and I saw from her profile that her home address is in Austin, TX. She was very pleasant, said she was in town for a few days visiting her sister. I asked if she wanted a coffee from our new machine—I’ve been offering it to everyone, honestly, it’s such a huge improvement over the old one—and she said yes, that would be lovely. She commented on how much better the traffic was today compared to yesterday, said her drive from her sister's place was only twenty minutes. While the coffee was brewing we chatted a bit about the weather.

She got right to the point after that. Said she wanted to make a fairly large payment on her Amazon Prime Visa (*7075). She had a cashier's check with her and slid it across the desk. I took a look at it, everything seemed in order, and I pulled up her card account on my screen. We made some small talk while the system was loading. She saw the Bay City Herons calendar on my cubicle wall and asked if I was a fan. I told her I was a lifelong supporter, and we spent a couple minutes talking about their chances this season. She seems to think they have a real shot if the new pitcher stays healthy, and I have to agree. It's always nice when a customer connects on something like that.

Anyway, I got her account up and initiated the credit card payment workflow. She handed me the check and I started keying in the details. I must have been a bit distracted by our chat about the Herons, because I typed in the payment amount as $2,030.00. I almost hit enter, but I have this habit of always double-checking the physical check against the screen before finalizing, and I'm glad I do. I saw the numbers were transposed. "Oh, whoops," I said, "my fingers are having a Monday." She laughed. I corrected the amount on the screen to the proper $2,300.00, verified it one more time against the check in my hand, and then processed the payment. I told her, "Okay, that's all set, your payment of $2,300.00 has been submitted."

The system generated the receipt, and I was about to print it when I started explaining the next steps. I told her that since she made the payment in-branch, it should have same-day availability and reflect on her available credit very soon. Standard talk. However, as I said that, a notification popped up on my screen showing the payment details. I saw the system had automatically placed a hold on the funds. I had to immediately correct myself. "Actually, Ms. Abara, I need to amend that. I apologize. Because this is a cashier's check, the system has placed a standard hold on the payment for verification. It looks like the funds will be fully applied and the hold will be released on April 20, 2026." She looked a little confused, so I explained that while cashier's checks are very secure, it's just a standard bank policy for fraud prevention. I even added that for very large checks, like anything over $5,000.00, the hold can sometimes be even longer, so this was just the normal procedure. She was perfectly fine with it, said it wasn't a problem at all and that she wasn't planning on making any big purchases right away anyway. She was just glad to have it taken care of. I printed out her receipt, making sure the confirmation number BRC-9795051 was clearly visible for her.

Just as I was handing her the receipt, she said, "Oh, one more quick question." She said her wife, Leonie, also has a card with us and she was wondering if she could make a payment on her behalf. She pulled out her phone to look up the number, saying, "I think the card ends in 4243." I explained that for security and privacy reasons, I couldn't accept a payment from her for an account that wasn't hers. Leonie would have to come into a branch herself with her ID, or she could of course make a payment online or through the mobile app. I didn't look up the card or confirm any details, just explained the policy. Aisha understood completely, said it made sense. She thanked me again for the coffee and the help. I walked her to the door and we wished the Bay City Herons good luck one more time. A very smooth and friendly interaction all around, even with my small data entry slip-up and the correction about the funds hold.

Follow-up:
No follow-up action required on my end. The payment of $2,300.00 was submitted successfully. Customer was informed of the funds hold and the release date of April 20, 2026. She left the Riverbend Plaza branch satisfied with the service. I will place the cashier's check in the batch for end-of-day processing. The inquiry about her wife's card (ending in 4243) was resolved by explaining bank policy; no action was taken or is needed.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. My name is David. Who am I speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, David. This is Nadia Ferreira.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Ferreira. Thanks for calling. To make sure I have the right account pulled up here, could I just get your date of birth, please?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s...

AGENT: Thank you. Just one moment while my system loads everything up for your account. Sometimes it can be a little slow on a Monday.

CUSTOMER: No problem.

AGENT: Okay, I see you’re in Minneapolis. Getting a bit of that early autumn chill yet? We’re finally getting a break from the heat down here.

CUSTOMER: Oh, you know it. It was perfect weather for the Riverdale Rovers game on Saturday, though. A bit crisp, but sunny. We won, so that helped.

AGENT: Ah, that’s great to hear. I’m not much of a follower myself but my brother-in-law never misses a game. Alright, looks like everything is loaded for me now. I have the Chase Sapphire Preferred card ending in six-zero-one-seven. How can I help you today, Ms. Ferreira?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s the one. Well, I’m hoping you can help. My card seems to be blocked or something. I was trying to buy some things online yesterday, and it just kept getting declined. I tried on the Home Depot website and then on Etsy, and both times, declined. I know there’s money in the account, so I don’t understand what the problem is.

AGENT: Okay, I can certainly look into that for you. It’s definitely frustrating when that happens. You said this was for online purchases?

CUSTOMER: Yes, just online. I haven’t tried it in a store.

AGENT: Right. And you’re currently at home in Minneapolis? No travel or anything like that?

CUSTOMER: No, no, I’m home. I haven’t left the state in months.

AGENT: Okay, thank you. Just a moment while I review the account activity. I’m just typing here, bear with me… hmm. Okay. I am seeing some notes here that I think explain what’s going on. It looks like you recently updated your mailing address with us, is that right?

CUSTOMER: Oh, yes. I did. I went into the branch, maybe Friday? Or Saturday. Saturday morning. We moved about a month ago and I kept forgetting to update it.

AGENT: Okay, I see that here. It looks like the change was recorded on Saturday to… let me see… 6120 Pine Court in Minneapolis.

CUSTOMER: That’s the one.

AGENT: Perfect. So, what I believe has happened here is a bit of a timing issue. When you update your address, it can sometimes take a little while—up to forty-eight hours, usually—for that new address to sync up with the separate security system we use for verifying online purchases. It's called the Address Verification Service, or AVS.

CUSTOMER: Okay… so what does that mean?

AGENT: It means that when you made those online orders yesterday, you correctly entered your new address, the one on Pine Court. But the AVS system, which the merchants check against, still had your old address on file. So when the two didn't match, the transactions were declined for security. I see the declines here, one at Etsy and one at Home Depot Online, both with a note that says 'AVS Mismatch'.

CUSTOMER: So it’s because I used my new address? That seems backward.

AGENT: I completely understand why it feels that way. It's a security measure to prevent fraud, but in cases like this, where there’s a recent, legitimate change, it can cause this exact problem. And… ah, okay, I see the second part of the issue now. Because there were several of these declines in a short period, our automated fraud detection system placed a temporary block on the card for any online or phone transactions. That's why nothing would go through after the first few attempts. Your card should still work fine for in-person, chip-and-PIN purchases, though.

CUSTOMER: So it *is* blocked. Can you unblock it? I have some other things I need to order.

AGENT: That’s the tricky part, and I do apologize for this. Because this block was triggered automatically by the security system, I’m not able to remove it from my end. It requires a different team to review the AVS sync and manually clear the block. What I need to do is open a case for them to get this resolved for you.

CUSTOMER: You can’t just fix it? I’m on the phone with you right now.

AGENT: I truly wish I could, Ms. Ferreira. I don't have the tools for this specific type of block. But I can get the process started immediately. I'll open a formal case, and that will get it in the queue for the right department to action. I’m creating that for you right now, and the reference number for your records is CASE-4636049.

CUSTOMER: And how long will that take?

AGENT: They are usually quite quick, but to be safe and to make sure you get a clear update, I can schedule a callback for you. We can have a specialist call you back once everything is confirmed to be working again. Would you like me to set that up?

CUSTOMER: I guess. Yes, please.

AGENT: Great. And what’s the best number for that callback?

CUSTOMER: Uh, you can call my office landline. It’s 612-555-0669. Wait, sorry, no, that’s not right. It’s 612-555-0696. The last two digits are nine-six.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me just read that back. A callback to an office landline at 612-555-0696. And I can schedule that for… let’s see… let’s book it for September 18, 2026. That should give them more than enough time to get it all sorted. How does that sound?

CUSTOMER: Fine. September 18th it is.

AGENT: Excellent. I'm putting all of this in the notes for case CASE-4636049. I am so sorry for the hassle this has caused you. For the inconvenience, I'd like to go ahead and apply a $35.00 courtesy credit to your account. Let me just process that for you now… one moment… hmm. That’s odd. You know what, Ms. Ferreira, it seems my system is rejecting the credit request. I'm not sure why. I am so sorry, it looks like I won’t be able to post that for you right now. I will add a strong note to the case file requesting the specialist to apply it for you once they resolve the main issue.

CUSTOMER: Of course. Figures. It’s just been one of those days with this card. My wife, Renata, her card works fine. The one ending in 8340. No issues at all.

AGENT: I understand your frustration completely. I have documented everything here. Is there anything else I can assist you with today while I have you?

CUSTOMER: Actually, yes. While I have you. I was looking at my statement online just before I called, and there’s a huge charge on there I don’t recognize at all. I think it was at Macy's? Let me… let me just pull it up again. Hold on.

AGENT: Please, take your time.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I have it. No, it wasn’t Macy’s. It says… ‘Crescent Moon Bookshop’. For six hundred and fifty-two dollars and thirty-one cents.

AGENT: Okay, I see that transaction. Crescent Moon Bookshop for $652.31. And the location is listed as Albuquerque, NM.

CUSTOMER: Albuquerque? I’ve never been to Albuquerque in my life. That is absolutely not mine.

AGENT: Understood. And just to confirm, is the physical card ending in 6017 in your possession right now?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s right here in my wallet.

AGENT: And you didn't authorize anyone else to use the card or the card number for this purchase?

CUSTOMER: Absolutely not.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming. This is definitely something we need to dispute. I can file that for you right now. We will open an investigation, and while we do that, we’ll issue a temporary credit for the disputed amount, so you won’t be responsible for it during the investigation.

CUSTOMER: Good. Thank you.

AGENT: Alright, I’m initiating the dispute now. The merchant is Crescent Moon Bookshop, amount is $652.31. Okay… just entering the details… and the reason code is, uh, DISPUTE_RC_13.1. Okay, that's filed. The reference number for this dispute is DSP-5614688. The investigation can take some time, but you'll receive letters or emails updating you on the progress.

CUSTOMER: DSP-5614688. Got it.

AGENT: And just as a procedural note, while you are not required to pay the disputed $652.31 while it's being investigated, the remainder of your statement balance is still due by the payment date. It’s important to know that late payments on any undisputed balance can incur a late fee of up to $41.00. But that shouldn't be an issue here.

CUSTOMER: Understood. So, just to be clear: you can’t fix my card for online shopping right now, but you’ve opened a case and someone will call me back on my office phone on the 18th. And you’ve started a dispute for that bookshop charge.

AGENT: That is a perfect summary, Ms. Ferreira. The case for the AVS block is CASE-4636049, with a callback scheduled to 612-555-0696 for September 18, 2026. And the fraud dispute for the charge in Albuquerque is filed under reference DSP-5614688. I've noted everything we discussed in your account.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Well, thank you for your help, David. I appreciate you getting that sorted out, at least.

AGENT: It's my pleasure, Ms. Ferreira. I'm sorry again that we couldn't get it all resolved for you on this one call. Is there anything else at all?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s everything.

AGENT: Alright then. Thank you for being a Chase customer, and I hope you have a much better rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.
