IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. Please listen carefully as our menu options have recently changed. To continue in English, press one. Para Español, oprima dos.
For credit card services, including activation, payments, and rewards, press one.
For checking or savings accounts, press two.
For technical support with our website or mobile app, press three.
For all other inquiries, press four.
<beep>
IVR: Please say or enter the last four digits of your credit card number.
<keypad tones>
IVR: Thank you. To protect your account, please say or enter your date of birth.
<keypad tones>
IVR: Thank you. Please hold while we connect you to the next available agent. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance.

HOLD MESSAGE: <upbeat instrumental music> Did you know you can earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend four thousand dollars on purchases in the first three months from account opening with the Chase Sapphire Preferred card? That’s over seven hundred dollars toward travel when you redeem through Chase Ultimate Rewards. Ask your agent for more details. <upbeat instrumental music continues>

AGENT: Thank you for calling Chase, you're speaking with Alex. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, my name is Hannah Costa.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Costa. How can I help you?

CUSTOMER: I... I am just at my wit's end here. I’ve been trying to log into my app for two days and it keeps saying my account is locked. And then yesterday I tried to buy groceries and my card was declined. My Chase Sapphire Reserve card. I'm just... I'm completely locked out of everything.

AGENT: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that, Ms. Costa. That sounds incredibly frustrating. I can definitely look into what's going on with the account for you. To start, I just need to verify your identity. I can see you entered some details into the phone system, but for security I'll need to confirm them. Can you please spell your full name for me?

IVR: Thank you for calling Chase. To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en español, oprima dos. Please say or enter your sixteen-digit card number.
CUSTOMER: [Muffled sounds, keypad tones]
IVR: I didn't get that. Please say or enter your card number, or say 'I don't have it'.
CUSTOMER: Representative.
IVR: Okay. To direct your call, please tell me the reason you're calling. You can say 'check my balance', 'report a lost card', or something else.
CUSTOMER: Account is frozen.
IVR: I understand you're calling about a frozen account. Please hold while I connect you to an agent. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with your Chase Sapphire Reserve card? For a limited time, get 5x points on dining purchases. From morning coffee to midnight snacks, every meal gets you closer to your next big adventure. Ask your agent for details or visit our website to learn more.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. You've reached Chase Card Services, my name is Maria. How can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: Hi Maria, I hope you can help. My account seems to be completely frozen. I can't log into the app, and my card got declined trying to buy something online. It's… it's been a couple of days now and it's getting really frustrating.

AGENT: I can certainly understand that, and I'll do my best to figure out what's going on. First, I just need to verify your identity to access the account. Can I start with your full name, please?

CUSTOMER: Sure. It's Jonah Mensah. M-E-N-S-A-H.

AGENT: Thank you, Mr. Mensah. Just pulling up your profile now… okay. And for the last step, could you please confirm the date of birth we have on file for you?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's... [muffled, spoken away from the phone] honey, what's my... oh, right. It’s [date spoken softly].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. That matches what I have here. Okay, so my system is just taking a moment to load all the details. Sometimes it can be a little slow on a Saturday. How's the weather out there in Seattle? I hear you guys have been getting a lot of rain.

CUSTOMER: Oh, you know it. It's the usual. Grey and drizzly. At least the Riverdale Rovers pulled off a win last night, so that's something. Were you watching?

AGENT: I missed it! I was working, but my brother was sending me updates. Sounds like it was a nail-biter right to the end. I’ll have to catch the highlights. Okay, looks like I have your account information up now. Let me see… I have your Chase Sapphire Reserve card ending in two-three-two-five. Is that the one we're talking about?

CUSTOMER: That's the one. My wife, Leonie, she's on the account too, and her card works just fine. Hers ends in, uh, 6428. She used it at the grocery store this morning. But mine, and the main account login, it's just completely locked down. I tried calling yesterday and couldn't get through the security questions, I guess I was just flustered. They told me I had to go to a branch, but I can't get to one until next week.

AGENT: Okay, I see. Yes, I do have some notes here that I'm reviewing. Thank you for your patience… hmm. Okay. So, Mr. Mensah, I can see what happened. It looks like our automated security system detected some unusual activity on your account a couple of days ago. Let me read you the note here. On September tenth, at about eight P.M. your time, it looks like there was a password reset and a change to the contact email address on the profile.

CUSTOMER: What? I didn't do that. What did it change to?

AGENT: I can see that, sir. The system flagged it because the login came from a device it didn't recognize in Newark, New Jersey. And since your home address is in Seattle, that distance triggered an immediate alert.

CUSTOMER: New Jersey? I've never even been to New Jersey. So someone hacked my account?

AGENT: It appears that someone may have gained unauthorized access to your credentials, yes. Our fraud detection system automatically fired what's called an Account Takeover rule. For your protection, it placed an immediate freeze on the account, which is what you're experiencing now. It suspended digital banking access and blocked your card for any transactions where the physical card isn't present. It also automatically rolled back that email address change, so your original email is still secure.

CUSTOMER: Okay, so that's good. But… so can you unfreeze it for me? I've got bills to pay.

AGENT: I completely understand your urgency, Mr. Mensah. And this is where it gets a little complicated. Because of the nature of this specific freeze—the ATO, or Account Takeover, freeze—it requires a review from our specialist fraud and security team. The note from your call yesterday is here as well, and it says that when the automated verification failed, the agent advised a branch visit because they also couldn't lift this particular hold. I'm unfortunately in the same position; frontline agents don't have the security permissions to remove this type of lock.

CUSTOMER: You're kidding me. So what am I supposed to do? Just wait until I can get to a branch? That's not for another four or five days. This is ridiculous.

AGENT: I know this is frustrating, and I truly do apologize for the inconvenience. What I can do for you right now is open a high-priority internal case for our review team. They will investigate the unauthorized access and once they've secured the account, they can lift the freeze. I can get that started for you immediately.

CUSTOMER: And how long does that take?

AGENT: They typically respond within two to three business days. To make sure you get an update, I can schedule a direct callback for you from one of the case managers. How about we set that up?

CUSTOMER: Yes, fine. Let's do that. At least it's something.

AGENT: Okay, I'm opening the case now. Just typing in the details… okay. The reference number for this case is CASE-6177174. I'll just repeat that: CASE-6177174.

CUSTOMER: Got it. CASE-6177174.

AGENT: Excellent. Now, for the callback. Our team will call you to provide an update or complete any final verification steps. The best number we have on file for you is a mobile number. Is that still the best place to reach you?

CUSTOMER: No, no, don't call the mobile. My signal is terrible at work. Can they call my office landline?

AGENT: Of course. What is that number?

CUSTOMER: It's 206-555-0320. Wait, no, sorry, I always do that. It's 206-555-0320, sorry, 206-555-0302. The last two digits are zero-two.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me read that back to you. The callback number is an office landline, 206-555-0302.

CUSTOMER: That's correct.

AGENT: And what would be a good date for them to call? They are available Monday to Friday.

CUSTOMER: Let's see… today's the twelfth. Let's give them a few days. How about… Thursday the nineteenth?

AGENT: September nineteenth… let me check the calendar. Yes, September 19, 2026 is a Thursday. That works perfectly. I've scheduled the callback for you for that afternoon.

CUSTOMER: Okay. Thank you. Um, actually, while I have you on the line… there was something else. I was looking at my last statement before all this happened, and there's a charge on there I don't recognize at all.

AGENT: I can certainly look into that for you. Do you have the details of the transaction?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, hold on, let me pull it up again. It was for… I think it was at Staples? Or something like that. Just a sec… no, that's not it. Here it is. It's for $285.50.

AGENT: Okay, $285.50. And do you see the name of the merchant?

CUSTOMER: Yes. It says… Brightline Fitness Club. In Tucson, Arizona. I have no idea what that is. I've never been to Tucson, and I definitely didn't join a gym there.

AGENT: I see. Brightline Fitness Club, Tucson, AZ, for $285.50. And you're certain neither you nor any authorized user on your account made this charge?

CUSTOMER: One hundred percent certain. It must be related to the hacking thing.

AGENT: It's very possible. We can definitely dispute this for you. I'm going to file a dispute claim right now. I just have to read you a quick disclosure. "When you submit a dispute, a temporary credit for the disputed amount may be applied to your account. We will investigate the claim with the merchant, which can take up to two billing cycles. Please note that failure to make the minimum payment on the undisputed portion of your balance may result in your account becoming past due, which can incur a late fee of up to $39.00." Do you understand and wish to proceed?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I understand. Go ahead.

AGENT: Perfect. I'm processing that now. The reason code I'm using is for a transaction that the cardholder does not recognize. Okay… the dispute has been filed. Your reference number for this is DSP-7233142.

CUSTOMER: DSP… okay, 7233142. Got it.

AGENT: And I've submitted that with the reason code DISPUTE_RC_13.3. You should see a temporary credit for the $285.50 post to your account within the next day or two while we investigate.

CUSTOMER: Okay, great. Well, thank you for handling that.

AGENT: You're very welcome. And Mr. Mensah, I know this has been a major headache for you, dealing with the account freeze and the fraudulent charge. To apologize for the trouble, I'd like to apply a $20.00 courtesy credit to your account. Let me just process that for you now… one moment.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thank you. I appreciate that.

AGENT: Just typing it in… and… huh. That's odd. It seems the system has rejected the credit. I'm very sorry, it looks like the account freeze is so comprehensive that it's blocking any kind of credit posting as well. I am so sorry about that. Once the security team lifts the freeze, that's something we can certainly revisit.

CUSTOMER: Of course it is. Figures. Okay, well, nothing to be done, I guess.

cust_synth_030:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Customer Jonah Mensah came into the Riverbend Plaza branch this afternoon, around two-ish. I recognized him right away, he comes in a few times a year to make a payment or handle other business. He always seems to be in a good mood, which is a nice change of pace. He was complaining about the traffic coming down from Seattle, said it took him almost an hour longer than usual, which sounds about right for a weekday afternoon. I offered him a coffee from our new machine – the one management finally approved after months of us asking for it – and he was happy to take one. Said it was a big improvement over the old one, and I have to agree.

He got right to business. He pulled a cashier's check out of an envelope and said he wanted to make a large payment toward his Chase Sapphire Reserve (*2325). I pulled up his profile and confirmed his identity with his driver's license, standard procedure. He was telling me about his plans for the card, some travel coming up later in the year. While he sipped his coffee, I took the check and started the payment process in the system. I must have been distracted by our conversation about the new coffee machine or the traffic, because I keyed in the payment as $4,400.00. I almost hit enter, but something felt off, so I glanced back down at the physical check in my hand to verify the amount. Big oops on my part. The check was clearly for $4,040.00. A simple fat-finger error, but a good reminder to slow down. I cancelled the entry and re-keyed it for the correct amount of $4,040.00. I double-checked it on the screen this time before proceeding.

I told him, "Okay, Mr. Mensah, we've got that payment of $4,040.00 going toward your Sapphire Reserve. Since it's a cashier's check, you should see that reflected with same-day availability on the balance." But of course, the system had other ideas. As soon as I processed the payment, a notification popped up informing me that a standard hold was being placed on the funds. I had to walk back what I just said, which is always a bit awkward. I explained to him that my initial comment was a bit too general, and that for certain non-cash transactions like a cashier's check, the system automatically applies a hold to allow time for the funds to clear properly. I clarified that this is a standard security measure and not specific to his account. I even mentioned that for very large cashier's checks, say anything over $10,000.00, the hold period can sometimes be even longer. He was very understanding about it. He just asked when the money would be fully available. I checked the hold details on my screen and confirmed for him that the hold is set to release on April 18, 2026, at which point the payment will be fully posted. I printed out his receipt and pointed out the transaction number, BRC-4299634, for his records.

After we finished with his payment, he had another question. He asked about his wife, Leonie. He said she also has a card with us and he wanted to know if he could make a payment for her while he was here. He thought her card ended in 5777. I had to explain that due to privacy and security policies, I couldn't access his wife's account information or process a transaction for her without her being present with her ID. I told him the easiest way for her to pay would be through the mobile app or online, but if she preferred to come in person, we'd be happy to help her at the Riverbend Plaza branch or any other location. He completely understood, said he figured that was the case but thought it was worth asking.

While the receipt was printing, we got to chatting about the Riverdale Rovers. He had a Rovers scarf on, so I figured he was a fan. He was really excited about their performance this season, especially with the new striker they picked up. We spent a good five minutes talking about their chances of making the playoffs. He thinks they're a sure thing, I'm a little more cautious. We both agreed last weekend's match was a nail-biter. It's always great when you can connect with a customer about something other than just banking. It makes the whole interaction feel more personal. He finished his coffee, thanked me for the help (and for the chat about the Riverdale Rovers), and headed out. Seemed perfectly happy with the outcome despite the small hiccup with the funds hold explanation.

Follow-up:
None needed. Customer payment was processed successfully for $4,040.00. The funds hold was explained and the customer understood the reason for the hold and the release date of April 18, 2026. The customer's secondary query about his wife's card was answered per bank policy. No further action is required from the branch.

cust_synth_032:LM3_BRANCH.body:
Mr. Daniel Okafor visited the Riverbend Plaza branch this afternoon, just after the lunch rush. He was in a good mood, said he was heading home to Portland a little early today and wanted to take care of a bill on his way out. He helped himself to a coffee from our new machine and commented on how much better it is than the old one, which is something we're hearing from a lot of clients. I couldn't agree more. After the usual pleasantries, I asked what I could help him with, and he said he needed to make a payment on his Chase Slate Edge (*6128) card. I pulled up his profile using his debit card and confirmed his identity with his Oregon driver's license, everything matched up perfectly.

He handed me a cashier's check to make the payment. While I was inspecting the check and getting the transaction screen ready, we got to talking about the Granite Falls Miners. He's a big fan, and so am I, so we spent a few minutes complaining about that heartbreaking loss over the weekend. He was saying their bullpen is looking shaky this season, and I had to agree. As he was giving me his theory on why the manager keeps making questionable pitching changes, I was keying in the payment details. I was a bit distracted by the conversation and my first entry for the payment amount was $1,250.00. Thankfully, before I hit the final confirmation, I did my standard second look, comparing the screen to the physical check in my hand. I immediately saw my mistake. The check was for $1,520.00. I let out a little "oops," and told him I'd nearly shorted him a few hundred dollars. He had a good laugh about it. I apologized for the typo and corrected the entry to the proper amount of $1,520.00, triple-checking it this time to be absolutely sure.

While the system was processing the corrected transaction, he said, "Hey, can I ask a quick question for my partner, Casey?" He wanted to know if he could also make a payment on Casey's card while he was here. He said he didn't have the card with him but he thought the number ended in 4647. I had to explain that unfortunately, due to privacy and security policies, I couldn't access an account or process a payment for a third party who wasn't present to provide identification. I let him know that Casey would either need to visit a branch in person, or they could use any of our other convenient channels like the app, online banking, or our automated phone system. He was very understanding and said, "No problem, that makes sense. I'll just tell them to do it online."

Once I submitted the payment for his Chase Slate Edge card, I told him that since he was making the payment in branch, it should have same-day availability and he'd see his available credit update very shortly. Famous last words. As soon as I said that, the system displayed a notification. A standard funds hold was being placed on the payment. I immediately had to correct myself. I apologized and explained that my initial statement was for cash or debit payments, but because he was using a cashier's check, it's subject to a routine verification hold. It's a non-negotiable system thing. I explained that the payment is still considered "posted" today, but the funds themselves won't be officially released and applied against his balance for a few business days. To give him some context, I noted that this is standard for most checks and that for very large cashier's checks, say anything over $7,500.00, the holds can sometimes be even longer, but his was just the normal, short-term hold. The system specified the exact date, so I was able to tell him the funds would be fully released on May 15, 2026. He was a little frustrated but seemed to get it once I explained it was a federal banking regulation and not a decision made at the branch.

To wrap things up, I printed his receipt, which had the reference number BRC-7875815. I took a moment to walk him through it, highlighting the confirmed payment amount of $1,520.00. I also pointed to the fine print regarding the funds hold and, just to be extra clear, I wrote down "Hold releases May 15, 2026" right on the receipt for him. He thanked me for being so thorough. We wished each other a good rest of the week and hoped the Granite Falls Miners would pull off a win in their next game. He headed out, seeming satisfied enough despite the hold situation.

Follow-up:
None required at this time. Customer was fully informed of the standard funds hold on his cashier's check payment and the specific release date of May 15, 2026. Customer understood it was a standard policy. Payment has been posted and will be fully applied upon hold release.

[Keypad tone]

IVR: Please enter the last four digits of your credit card, followed by the pound key.

[Keypad tones]

IVR: Thank you. Please hold while we connect you to the next available agent. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can earn even more with your Amazon Prime Visa card? For a limited time, get 5x points on dining at your favorite restaurants. From morning coffee to date night dinner, every meal gets you closer to your next reward. Ask your agent for more details.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is Alex. I'm looking at the card ending in six-eight-two-four. Am I speaking with the primary cardholder today?

CUSTOMER: Yes, you are. Hi. My name is Ingrid Okafor. I hope you can help me.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Okafor. I'll certainly do my best. Before we get into it, I just need to quickly verify your identity for security. Can I get your full name again, please?

CUSTOMER: Of course. It’s Ingrid Okafor. I-N-G-R-I-D, Okafor, O-K-A-F-O-R.

AGENT: Thank you. And could you please confirm your date of birth for me?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s [REDACTED].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you. And one last thing, can you confirm the billing address I have on file, including the zip code?

CUSTOMER: Yep, it’s [REDACTED] San Diego, CA, [REDACTED].

AGENT: Excellent, thank you so much for that. Just give me one moment here, Ms. Okafor, my system is loading up your account details. It can be a little… a little slow on a Monday morning.

AGENT: Just taking a second here… So, how's the weather down in San Diego today? I bet it’s better than the rain we have here.

AGENT: Ha! You saw the game on Saturday? What a disaster that was. I couldn't believe it when they missed that penalty.

CUSTOMER: Oh my god, right? I was screaming at the TV. My husband, Gustavo, he just walked out of the room. He said he couldn't take the stress anymore.

AGENT: Northwind Home Audio. Okay, I see it. Is the amount six hundred and twenty-two dollars and seventy-nine cents?

AGENT: I'm looking at the transaction details here. It looks like this charge was processed two days ago. The location is listed as Richmond, Virginia.

CUSTOMER: Richmond, Virginia? Are you serious? I’ve never been to Virginia in my life! I’m in San Diego! I haven't left the state in over a year. This is definitely not me.

AGENT: Okay, thank you for confirming that. That’s an important detail. So you didn’t make this purchase, and you weren't in Richmond, VA.

CUSTOMER: Okay… so that forty-one dollars has nothing to do with me?

AGENT: Correct. It is not a fee on your account. It's just a script I am required to read before proceeding with certain account actions. My apologies for any confusion.

CUSTOMER: No, it's fine. Go ahead with the dispute.

AGENT: Alright. I am now initiating a dispute for the charge of $622.79 from Northwind Home Audio. I am marking the reason as cardholder does not recognize the transaction. CUSTOMER: So what happens now? Do they take the charge off?

AGENT: The dispute process has officially begun. While the investigation is open, you are not responsible for paying the disputed amount. We will work with the merchant's bank to investigate. CUSTOMER: D… S… P… dash… can you repeat that?

AGENT: Of course. D as in David, S as in Sam, P as in Paul, dash, four-five-seven-zero-four-two-one.

CUSTOMER: Got it. DSP-4570421. Thank you. This is all just… so stressful.

AGENT: I completely understand, Ms. Okafor. It's very unsettling to see something like this on your account. I see you've been a loyal cardmember for a very long time. Let me just try and process that for you now.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Well, thank you. I appreciate that.

AGENT: You’re very welcome. I’m just clicking through the screens here… one moment… Hmm. Oh, for goodness sake. Ms. Okafor, I am so sorry. CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay. Well, don’t worry about it. It’s not your fault. The main thing is getting that huge charge sorted out.

AGENT: Absolutely. And we are on it. To make sure everything is properly tracked and that you receive follow-up, I'm also going to open an internal case file. This will link the dispute and all of our notes from this call together. That case number is CASE-4646705.

CUSTOMER: Okay, another number. C-A-S-E…

AGENT: Yes, dash, four-six-four-six-seven-zero-five. This is more for our internal tracking, but you can certainly have it for your records.

CUSTOMER: Four-six-four-six-seven-zero-five. Got it.

AGENT: Perfect. Now, what I'd like to do is schedule a callback for you. We can have an agent from our dispute resolution team call you back with an update. We can set it for about a week from now, which should give them some time to have initial findings. How does that sound?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that would be great. A call would be very helpful.

AGENT: Excellent. The system is suggesting a callback on September 14, 2026. Is that date okay for you?

CUSTOMER: September 14… yes, that’s a Monday. That should be fine.

AGENT: Great. And what is the best number to reach you at? I see a mobile number on file, is that the best one?

CUSTOMER: You know, I’ll be at work that day. Could you call my office landline instead? I don’t like taking personal calls on my mobile when I’m in the office.

AGENT: Of course. I can add a temporary number for the callback. What is that office number?

CUSTOMER: It’s 619-555-0805.

AGENT: Okay, I have 619-555-0805. Let me just confirm…

CUSTOMER: Oh! Wait, wait, I’m so sorry. I always do that. It’s 619-555-0850. The last two digits are five-zero. My apologies, I transpose them all the time. It’s 619-555-0850.

AGENT: Not a problem at all, happens to the best of us. Thank you for clarifying. So, I have the callback scheduled for September 14, 2026, to your office landline at 619-555-0850. Is that all correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s all correct. Thank you so much.

AGENT: You are very welcome. So, to recap our call today, Ms. Okafor: we have successfully filed a dispute for the charge of $622.79 from Northwind Home Audio. That dispute number is DSP-4570421. The reason code used was DISPUTE_RC_10.4. We've also opened a master case to track this, CASE-4646705. And I have scheduled a callback for you on September 14, 2026, to your office landline. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s everything. You’ve been very helpful, Alex. Thank you.

AGENT: It was my pleasure, Ms. Okafor. I'm glad I could get this started for you. Please don't worry, our team will take it from here. Thank you for calling, and I hope the Riverdale Rovers give us something to cheer about next weekend.

CUSTOMER: Ha! Me too. You have a good day.

AGENT: You too. Goodbye.

IVR: Thank you for calling Chase Card Services. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. To continue in English, press one. Para continuar en español, oprima dos.

IVR: Please say or enter your sixteen-digit card number.

IVR: Thank you. For security, please enter the four-digit year you were born.

IVR: Thank you. Main menu. To hear your account balance and recent transactions, press one. To make a payment, press two. To report a card lost, stolen, or to dispute a transaction, press three. For rewards, travel services, or other questions, press four. To hear these options again, press nine.

IVR: You have selected "dispute a transaction." Please hold while we connect you to the next available agent. Your estimated wait time is two minutes.

HOLD MESSAGE: Did you know you can manage your account anytime at chase.com? View statements, pay your bill, and set up alerts with just a few clicks. And don't forget about our exciting new offers! With the Chase Freedom Unlimited card, you can earn 5x points on dining, travel purchased through the Chase portal, and at drugstores. Ask your representative for more details. We value your business and will be with you shortly.

AGENT: Thank you for holding, my name is Alex. You're speaking with the Fraud Prevention department. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, yes, my name is Nadia Kaplan.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Kaplan. I can definitely help you out today. Just to be sure I have the right account pulled up here... for security purposes, can you please verify your date of birth?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it's [redacted].

AGENT: Perfect, thank you so much for that. One moment while my system loads everything up here. I see I'm looking at the Chase Ink Business Cash account ending in... four-zero-four-five. Is that the card we're talking about today?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's the one. The *4045.

AGENT: Great. Just takes a second to... get everything populated. It’s a little slow on my end today, my apologies.

CUSTOMER: No problem.

AGENT: How's your day going so far in Phoenix? Looks like you're calling from... yeah, the Phoenix area. Must be getting hot already.

CUSTOMER: Oh, you have no idea. We're already hitting triple digits. The AC is working overtime. How about you?

AGENT: Can't complain, pretty mild over here. We had that big storm roll through last night, so it's cooled things down. Hey, are you a Herons fan, by any chance? The Bay City Herons?

CUSTOMER: You know, I don't follow baseball that closely, but my husband does. He was pretty upset about the game last night.

AGENT: Ah, tell me about it. That last inning was a heartbreaker. Total collapse. Anyway... okay! Looks like my system is finally caught up. Thank you for your patience, Ms. Kaplan. So, what can I help you with regarding the account today?

CUSTOMER: I was looking at my last statement and there's a charge on there that I absolutely do not recognize. It's for a pretty big amount.

AGENT: Okay, I can definitely look into that for you. That’s exactly what we're here for. Do you have the statement in front of you?

CUSTOMER: I do, I do. I have it up on my screen. It’s… um… let me see. The charge is from… I think it was at Burlington? Something like that. It just doesn't sound familiar at all.

AGENT: Burlington. Okay, I'm not seeing a recent charge from a merchant with that name, but sometimes the names on the statement can be a little different from the storefront name. Can you tell me the exact date and the amount of the charge?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the amount was... six hundred and one dollars and forty-nine cents.

AGENT: Okay, $601.49. And the date?

CUSTOMER: It posted on... August twenty-seventh.

AGENT: August twenty-seventh. Okay. Hmm. Let me just filter by that amount. One second... Okay, I do see it. A charge for $601.49. The merchant name I see here on my end is… let's see… Maple & Main Furniture. Does that sound any more familiar?

CUSTOMER: Oh! You know what, you're right. I was looking at the wrong line. My apologies. Yes, it says that here too. Maple & Main Furniture.

AGENT: No problem at all. And the location on that transaction shows as Richmond, VA.

CUSTOMER: Richmond, VA? No. Absolutely not. I've never even been to Virginia. I'm in Phoenix. I haven't left the state in over a year.

AGENT: Okay. And you're certain no one else is authorized on this business account who might have made the purchase?

CUSTOMER: No. It's just me. My brother Emeka has his own business card, but it’s a totally separate account. His works fine, the one ending in 7078, he's never had a single issue. But this card is only used by me. And I definitely did not buy six hundred dollars worth of furniture from a place in Richmond.

AGENT: Understood. I completely understand. It definitely sounds like a fraudulent charge. So, what we need to do is file a dispute. I can start that process for you right now. It's pretty straightforward. While I'm getting the initial forms ready, I am required to read you a brief disclosure. Just a moment.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

AGENT: This is just a general notice. Please be aware that if a payment is not received by the due date, your account may be subject to standard penalties. Late payments can incur a late fee of up to $41.00 and may be reported to credit bureaus. This is just a general policy notification. Okay, I'm back. So, what we'll do is file this claim. I'm going to lock your current card to prevent any further fraudulent activity, and we'll have a new card with a new number sent out to you. It should arrive in about five to seven business days.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that's fine. So what happens with the charge?

AGENT: Great question. Once I file the dispute, we'll issue a temporary credit to your account for the full amount, the $601.49, while we investigate. The investigation can take some time, but you won't be responsible for the charge during that period.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that's a relief.

AGENT: Absolutely. And for all the trouble this has caused, Ms. Kaplan, I'm going to go ahead and apply a $30.00 courtesy credit to your account for the inconvenience. Just as a thank you for your patience while we sort this out.

CUSTOMER: Oh, wow. Thank you, I appreciate that.

AGENT: You are very welcome. Let me just process that credit for you... one moment please... just have to click through a few screens here... okay... hmm. That’s odd. Ah. It looks like my system isn't allowing the credit to go through right now. I'm so sorry about that, it seems there's a system flag here... it looks like you're not eligible for a courtesy credit at this moment. So just to be clear, that $30.00 credit will not be posting to your account. I do apologize for mentioning it before confirming.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay. Well, that's fine. The main thing is the big charge.

AGENT: Exactly. My apologies again. So, let's get back to the dispute itself. I am now officially filing the dispute claim for the charge from Maple & Main Furniture. The amount is $601.49. And... okay, it's submitted. The reference number for this specific dispute is DSP-2035182. I can repeat that for you if you'd like to write it down.

CUSTOMER: Yes, please. D-S-P...

AGENT: Correct. DSP, as in dispute, dash, two-zero-three-five-one-eight-two.

CUSTOMER: Got it. DSP-2035182.

AGENT: Perfect. Internally, I've filed this with the reason code DISPUTE_RC_13.3, which is our code for a card-not-present fraudulent transaction, which matches what you've described. Now, to make sure this is all tracked properly on our end and that you have a single point of reference for any future calls, I'm also opening a master case file to link the dispute and the new card shipment.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

AGENT: That case number is CASE-5695236.

CUSTOMER: Okay, can you repeat that one too?

AGENT: Of course. It’s CASE, dash, five-six-nine-five-two-three-six.

CUSTOMER: Five-six-nine-five-two-three-six. Okay, I have it.

AGENT: Great. So, the investigation will now proceed. We'll contact the merchant and go through the verification process. We may need to follow up with you, and we also like to schedule a proactive callback just to check in and let you know the status. Would you like me to schedule a follow-up call for you?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that would be great.

AGENT: Okay. And what is the best number for us to reach you at for that callback?

CUSTOMER: Uh, yes. You can call my office line. It's 602-555-0818.

AGENT: Okay, I have 602-555-0818.

CUSTOMER: Oh, wait, sorry, no. My mistake. I always mix those last two up. It's 602-555-0881. The last digit is a one.

AGENT: Not a problem at all, thanks for catching that. Let me correct it. So that's 602-555-0881. And that's your office landline, correct? This won't change the mobile number we have on file for alerts.

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's the one. My office landline. Don't change my mobile.

AGENT: Perfect. Got it. Now, let me look at the calendar... we usually schedule these about two weeks out to give the investigation some time to progress. How does... let's see... Thursday, September 17, 2026 sound? We can have an agent call you on that day to provide an update.

CUSTOMER: September 17, 2026. Yes, that works for me.

AGENT: Excellent. I have now scheduled that callback. So, just to recap everything for you, Ms. Kaplan. We have filed dispute DSP-2035182 for the charge of $601.49 from Maple & Main Furniture. We have opened case CASE-5695236 to track this issue. Your current card ending in *4045 is now locked, and a new one is being mailed to your address on file. And finally, we have a callback scheduled for you on September 17, 2026 at your office number, 602-555-0881. Does that all sound correct?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that's everything. Thank you so much for your help.

AGENT: It was my pleasure, Ms. Kaplan. I know this kind of thing is stressful, but we'll get it sorted out for you. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that's it. You've been very helpful.

AGENT: You're very welcome. Thank you for calling Chase Fraud Prevention, and I hope the rest of your day is a lot less eventful. And tell your husband I'm hoping the Herons can pull it together for the next game!

CUSTOMER: (laughs) I will. Thanks again. Bye.

AGENT: Goodbye.

CUSTOMER: I do, I do. I have it up on my screen. It’s… um… let me see. The charge is from… I think it was at Burlington? Something like that. It just doesn't sound familiar at all.

AGENT: Burlington. Okay, I'm not seeing a recent charge from a merchant with that name, but sometimes the names on the statement can be a little different from the storefront name. Can you tell me the exact date and the amount of the charge?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the amount was... six hundred and one dollars and forty-nine cents.

AGENT: Okay, $601.49. And the date?

CUSTOMER: It posted on... August twenty-seventh.

AGENT: August twenty-seventh. Okay. Hmm. Let me just filter by that amount. One second... Okay, I do see it. A charge for $601.49. The merchant name I see here on my end is… let's see… Maple & Main Furniture. Does that sound any more familiar?

CUSTOMER: Oh! You know what, you're right. I was looking at the wrong line. My apologies. Yes, it says that here too. Maple & Main Furniture.

AGENT: No problem at all. And the location on that transaction shows as Richmond, VA.

CUSTOMER: Richmond, VA? No. Absolutely not. I've never even been to Virginia. I'm in Phoenix. I haven't left the state in over a year.

AGENT: Okay. And you're certain no one else is authorized on this business account who might have made the purchase?

CUSTOMER: No. It's just me. My brother Emeka has his own business card, but it’s a totally separate account. His works fine, the one ending in 7078, he's never had a single issue. But this card is only used by me. And I definitely did not buy six hundred dollars worth of furniture from a place in Richmond.

AGENT: Understood. I completely understand. It definitely sounds like a fraudulent charge. So, what we need to do is file a dispute. I can start that process for you right now. It's pretty straightforward. While I'm getting the initial forms ready, I am required to read you a brief disclosure. Just a moment.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

AGENT: This is just a general notice. Please be aware that if a payment is not received by the due date, your account may be subject to standard penalties. I'm going to lock your current card to prevent any further fraudulent activity, and we'll have a new card with a new number sent out to you. It should arrive in about five to seven business days.

AGENT: Great question. Once I file the dispute, we'll issue a temporary credit to your account for the full amount, the $601.49, while we investigate. The investigation can take some time, but you won't be responsible for the charge during that period.

CUSTOMER: Okay, that's a relief.

AGENT: Absolutely. And for all the trouble this has caused, Ms. Kaplan, I'm going to go ahead and apply a $30.00 courtesy credit to your account for the inconvenience. Just as a thank you for your patience while we sort this out.

CUSTOMER: Oh, wow. Thank you, I appreciate that.

AGENT: You are very welcome. Let me just process that credit for you... one moment please... just have to click through a few screens here... okay... hmm. That’s odd. Ah. It looks like my system isn't allowing the credit to go through right now. I'm so sorry about that, it seems there's a system flag here... it looks like you're not eligible for a courtesy credit at this moment. So just to be clear, that $30.00 credit will not be posting to your account. I do apologize for mentioning it before confirming.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay. Well, that's fine. The main thing is the big charge.

AGENT: Exactly. My apologies again. So, let's get back to the dispute itself. I am now officially filing the dispute claim for the charge from Maple & Main Furniture. The amount is $601.49. And... okay, it's submitted. The reference number for this specific dispute is DSP-2035182. I can repeat that for you if you'd like to write it down.

CUSTOMER: Yes, please. D-S-P...

AGENT: Correct. DSP, as in dispute, dash, two-zero-three-five-one-eight-two.

CUSTOMER: Got it. DSP-2035182.

CUSTOMER: Okay.

CUSTOMER: Okay, can you repeat that one too?

AGENT: Of course. It’s CASE, dash, five-six-nine-five-two-three-six.

AGENT: Thank you for holding. My name is David. Who am I speaking with today?

CUSTOMER: Hi, David. My name is Priya Patel.

AGENT: Hello, Ms. Patel. Thank you for calling. For security, I just need to verify a few details on the account. Can I please have your full name as it appears on your statement?

CUSTOMER: Yes, it’s Priya Patel. P-R-I-Y-A, Patel, P-A-T-E-L.

AGENT: Got it. Thank you. And could you please confirm the date of birth on the account?

CUSTOMER: [DOB stated]

AGENT: Perfect. And the billing address, just the street and city, please.

CUSTOMER: It’s… uh… it’s in Nashville, Tennessee.

AGENT: Okay, I see that here. Thank you so much for verifying that information, Ms. Patel. Just give my system here one moment to pull up all your account details. It can be a little… a little slow on a Monday.

CUSTOMER: No problem. I understand.

AGENT: So, while we wait for this to load, how’s the weather down there in Nashville today?

CUSTOMER: Oh, it’s hot! Really muggy. You know how it is here in the summer. Feels like you could swim through the air.

AGENT: I hear that. I’m up north and it’s just rain, rain, rain today. I’d almost trade you. Did you happen to catch the Bay City Herons game last night? That was a real nail-biter.

CUSTOMER: Oh, I did! My husband and I were yelling at the TV. I can't believe they pulled it off in the last few minutes. That final play was incredible.

AGENT: Right? I thought for sure they were done for. What a comeback. Okay, looks like… yep, there we go. I have your account information up now. So, Ms. Patel, how can I help you today?

CUSTOMER: I was looking at my online statement this morning and there’s a charge on there that I don’t recognize at all. It’s a pretty big one.

AGENT: Okay, I can definitely help you look into that. Do you have the details of the charge handy?

CUSTOMER: Um, yeah, I think so. I have the page open. I think… I think it was at Marshalls? Something like that. It just doesn’t look right.

AGENT: Marshalls, you said? Okay, I'm looking at your recent transactions now. Can you tell me the date and the amount?

CUSTOMER: Let me scroll… oh, wait, here it is. No, I’m sorry, it wasn't Marshalls, I was looking at the wrong line. Okay, the one I’m worried about says… it says 'Riverside Auto Glass'.

AGENT: Riverside Auto Glass. Okay. And what is the amount of that charge?

CUSTOMER: It's for five hundred and nine dollars and seventy cents.

AGENT: So that’s $509.70. And do you see a location for that merchant?

CUSTOMER: Yeah, it says Salt Lake City, UT. I’ve never even heard of that place.

AGENT: Okay, Ms. Patel, I’m seeing that transaction right here. It posted two days ago. A charge for $509.70 at Riverside Auto Glass in Salt Lake City, Utah. Do you have your Chase Sapphire Reserve card with you now? The one ending in star sixty-four fourteen?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I have it right here in my wallet.

AGENT: And have you traveled to Utah recently, or perhaps made any online purchases for auto parts or services?

CUSTOMER: No, absolutely not. I haven’t been to Utah in… gosh, probably ten years. And I definitely didn't buy any auto glass. My car is fine. It’s so strange, my sister Yuki's card works just fine, the one ending in 6833, no weird charges on hers. We were just talking about it.

AGENT: I understand. Well, based on what you’re telling me—that you have your card in your possession and you didn’t authorize this charge—it certainly sounds like fraudulent activity. What we need to do is file a dispute.

CUSTOMER: Okay. What does that involve?

AGENT: It’s a straightforward process on your end. I’ll file the claim right now. We’ll place a temporary credit on your account for the disputed amount while our fraud department investigates the transaction with the merchant. It usually takes a few business days for that credit to appear. Is it alright if I place you on a brief hold for about two or three minutes while I initiate that filing?

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s fine. Thank you.

AGENT: Perfect. I’ll be back with you shortly. Please hold.

[hold music]

AGENT: Ms. Patel? Thank you so much for holding.

CUSTOMER: I’m here.

AGENT: Great. So, I'm just filling out the last bits of the dispute form now. It’s processing. And for the inconvenience this has caused you, looking through your statements and having to call in, I'm going to go ahead and apply a $15.00 courtesy credit to your account. That should show up in the next day or so.

CUSTOMER: Oh, thank you. I appreciate that.

AGENT: Of course. The system is just… thinking about it. Okay. Just while this is saving, I am required to inform you that for general account management, any payments not received by the due date can incur a late fee of up to $41.00. I just have to read that disclosure. That's just a standard disclosure, it doesn't apply to your account status right now, everything looks in good order on your end.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I understand.

AGENT: Alright, it looks like the dispute filing was successful. I have a reference number for you for your records. Do you have a pen and paper handy?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I do. Go ahead.

AGENT: Okay, the dispute reference number is DSP, as in dispute, dash, four six seven three three eight zero.

CUSTOMER: Okay, let me read that back. D-S-P, dash, 4673380.

AGENT: That is correct. I have also opened an internal case to track the progress of this investigation from start to finish. That case number is CASE, C-A-S-E, dash, seven nine seven seven two four five.

CUSTOMER: Okay, case number… dash… 7977245.

AGENT: Perfect. And just for the record, the internal reason code we've filed this under is DISPUTE_RC_12.6. You don’t need to write that down, but it’s in the file. So, the next step is our investigation. Now, I’m just trying to finalize that credit for you… and… oh, huh. It seems the system isn't letting me apply that $15.00 courtesy credit right now. There's a system flag on dispute-related credits that seems to be blocking it. I'm very sorry about that, it looks like it will not post to the account after all. My apologies for mentioning it prematurely.

CUSTOMER: Oh. Okay, well, the main thing is the big charge.

AGENT: Absolutely. And that is being handled. So, our team will investigate, and we should have a resolution for you within the next week or two. I’d like to schedule a callback to go over the final outcome with you. Would that be helpful?

CUSTOMER: Yes, please.

AGENT: Okay. We can schedule that for a few weeks out to make sure the case is fully resolved. How does September 14, 2026 sound?

CUSTOMER: September… 14th? Yes, that works for me.

AGENT: Great. And what's the best number for us to call you back on?

CUSTOMER: You can reach me at my office. The number is 615-555-0850… oh, wait, sorry, I always mix those last two up. It's 615-555-0805.

AGENT: No problem at all. Let me just correct that here. Okay, got it. So I'll read that back to you. I have a callback scheduled for you on September 14, 2026, to the number 615-555-0805. And that's an OFFICE LANDLINE number, is that correct? I'm not changing the mobile number we have on file for alerts or anything.

CUSTOMER: Yes, that’s correct. It’s my work landline. Don't change my mobile.

AGENT: Perfect. That is all set up for you, Ms. Patel. So, to recap: we have successfully filed dispute DSP-4673380 for the $509.70 charge. A temporary credit will be issued to your account. And we have opened case CASE-7977245 to track this, with a callback scheduled to your office landline for September 14, 2026. Is there anything else at all I can assist you with today?

CUSTOMER: No, that’s everything. Thank you so much for your help, David.

AGENT: You are very welcome, Ms. Patel. Thank you for your call, and have a great rest of your day.

CUSTOMER: You too. Bye.
